01.1Chapter 1 — Knowledge graphs and LLMs: A killer combination

Knowledge graph kya hai

Knowledge graph information ko nodes aur relationships ki shape me rakhta hai — jaise dimaag me concepts jude hote hain, waise hi data me entities judi hoti hain. Do nodes aur ek relationship se shuru hota hai; phir nodes badhte hain, relationships badhte hain, aur poora domain ek graph ban jata hai.

Nodes, relationships, properties

Har node ek entity hota hai — koi vyakti, jagah, dawa, bimari, company, ya koi bhi cheez jiske baare me baat ho rahi hai. Relationships batate hain ki do entities ke beech kya connection hai — jaise ek vyakti gaadi chalata hai (DRIVES), ya ek company kisi project ki owner hai (OWNS). Node aur relationship dono ke andar properties hoti hain — naam, date, brand, model, ya koi bhi detail.

Book ka pehla example ek healthcare knowledge graph hai: bimariyan, dawaaiyan, genes aur symptoms nodes hain, aur unke beech TREATS, CAUSES, ASSOCIATED_WITH jaise relationships hain. Ek hi graph me poori medical duniya ki picture ban jati hai — aur sawaal poochhna asaan ho jata hai, jaise "is bimari ka ilaaj kaunsi dawa karti hai?"

Term kahan se aaya

"Knowledge graph" term 1972 me ek Austrian linguist ne coin kiya tha, aur uske baad is par bahut academic research hui. Aam taur par popular yeh 2012 me hua, jab ek bade search engine ne web ka searchable Knowledge Graph representation banaya jo basic text search se behtar tha. Us company ka PageRank algorithm bhi graph-based proximity metrics se inspired tha — connected data ki value ko reinforce karta hai.

Aaj DBpedia, Wikidata aur YAGO jaise bade public knowledge graphs hain, aur Google, Amazon, Microsoft jaise companies apne products me knowledge graphs use karti hain. Voice assistants, search engines, recommendation systems — har jagah peeche ek graph kaam kar raha hota hai.

Graph database kyun

Relational database me relationships navigate karne ke liye expensive joins chahiye hote hain. Graph database connections ko directly traverse karta hai — isse deep, complex data ki querying tez aur efficient hoti hai. Fraud detection jaise use cases me multi-hop relationships ki rapid traversal chahiye hoti hai, jo graph me natural hai. Isi liye knowledge graph sirf ek data model nahi, ek poora approach hai: data ko waisa store karo jaisa woh duniya me connected hai.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: Knowledge graph ka power relationships me hai, nodes me nahi. Do alag databases me same entities ho sakti hain — farak sirf itna hai ki graph unke beech ke connections ko first-class citizen banata hai.
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 1 — Chapter 1

01.2Chapter 1 — Knowledge graphs and LLMs: A killer combination

Large language models kya hain

Large language model (LLM) ek neural network hai jo bahut bade text corpus par train hota hai aur language ko statistically samajhta hai. Woh words me nahi, word vectors me sochta hai — text ko semantic chunks me tod kar multidimensional space me unke beech ke statistical relationships map karta hai.

LLM kaise kaam karta hai

LLM ka core kaam simple hai: diye gaye context ke baad agla word predict karna. Lekin is simple kaam ko billions of parameters aur trillions of words par train karne se ek aisi capability nikalti hai jo translation, summarization, question answering, code generation — lagbhag har NLP task — kar sakti hai. Transformer architecture ne yeh possible banaya: attention mechanism har word ko sentence ke baaki words ke context me samajhta hai.

Transfer learning LLM ki sabse badi taakat hai. Ek model jo general text par train hua hai, use chhote se domain-specific dataset par fine-tune karke naye kaam ke liye taiyaar kiya ja sakta hai. Isse har task ke liye months tak custom dataset aur model banana band ho gaya — 2022 ke end me GPT-3.5 ke release ke baad yeh shift poori industry me dikha.

LLM ki limits — kyun akela kaafi nahi

LLM powerful hai, lekin magic solution nahi hai. Uske paas teen badi kamzoriyan hain. Pehli, hallucination: jab specialized ya precise factual knowledge chahiye aur woh grounded na ho, to model confident dikhne wala galat jawab bana deta hai. Doosri, knowledge cutoff: training ke baad ki duniya ke baare me use kuch pata nahi hota, aur nayi knowledge daalna mushkil hai. Teesri, opacity: jawab kahan se aaya, kis source par based hai — yeh batana LLM ke liye mushkil hai.

Enterprise production scenarios me yeh limits serious ho jati hain. Customer support, healthcare, finance — jahan galat jawab ka cost zyada hai, wahan LLM ko grounded, verifiable aur up-to-date knowledge chahiye hoti hai. Yahi woh jagah hai jahan knowledge graph kaam aata hai.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: LLM language ka expert hai, facts ka nahi. Woh bol sakta hai, lekin sach bolne ke liye use structured sach chahiye — aur woh sach knowledge graph deta hai.
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 1 — Chapter 1

01.3Chapter 1 — Knowledge graphs and LLMs: A killer combination

KG aur LLM — saath me zyada strong

Knowledge graph aur LLM ek doosre ki kamzoriyon ko cover karte hain. KG structured, verifiable, up-to-date knowledge deta hai; LLM us knowledge ko natural language me samajhta, jodta aur present karta hai. Dono ko jodne ka naam hai hybrid intelligent system.

Dono ki taakat, ek system me

KG ki taakat structure me hai: entities aur relationships explicit hain, human-readable hain, aur query kiye ja sakte hain. Koi bhi fact graph me trace kiya ja sakta hai — kis source se aaya, kab update hua. LLM ki taakat language me hai: woh unstructured text samajhta hai, context jodta hai, aur natural jawab deta hai. Dono mil kar woh kar sakte hain jo akela koi nahi kar sakta.

Book me chaar tareeke bataye gaye hain jinse dono ek doosre ko support karte hain. KG, LLM ki madad se: LLM unstructured text se entities aur relationships extract karke KG banana me madad karta hai. LLM, KG ki madad se: KG LLM ko grounded context deta hai, jisse hallucination kam hoti hai. KG, LLM ke bina: traditional methods se KG banta hai — ontology, rules, structured data. LLM, KG ke bina: sirf apne training data par bharosa karta hai — yahi hallucination ka source hai.

Killer combination kyun

Is combination ko "killer" isliye kaha gaya hai kyunki yeh do alag duniyaon ko jodta hai: symbolic AI (explicit knowledge, reasoning, rules) aur neural AI (statistical learning, language, pattern recognition). Symbolic AI verifiable hai lekin rigid hai; neural AI flexible hai lekin opaque hai. Dono ka hybrid woh system banata hai jo explainable bhi hai aur adaptable bhi.

Isi hybrid approach par poori book khadi hai. Aage ke chapters me hum pehle KG banana seekhenge, phir ML on graphs, aur phir KG-powered RAG aur question-answering agents — har jagah dono technologies saath kaam karti hain.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 1 — Chapter 1
← PreviousLarge language models kya hainNext →Data-driven applications me paradigm shift
01.4Chapter 1 — Knowledge graphs and LLMs: A killer combination

Data-driven applications me paradigm shift

Pehle data-driven application banane ka matlab hota tha: data collect karo, model train karo, deploy karo. Ab paradigm badal gaya hai — data ko knowledge me convert karna, aur knowledge ko LLM ke saath jod kar intelligent system banana, yeh naya tareeka hai.

Knowledge graph ke chaar pillars

Book knowledge graph ko chaar pillars par khada batati hai. Pehla — data integration: alag-alag sources se data ek unified graph me aata hai. Doosra — knowledge representation: domain ka meaning explicit schema aur ontology me capture hota hai. Teesra — reasoning: graph par rules aur algorithms chal kar naya knowledge infer kiya ja sakta hai. Chautha — exploration aur analytics: graph ko navigate, query aur visualize kiya ja sakta hai.

Yeh chaar pillars mil kar KG ko sirf ek database se zyada banate hain — ek aisa platform jahan data, meaning, reasoning aur discovery ek saath hote hain. Traditional data warehouse me data hota hai; knowledge graph me data ke saath uska matlab bhi hota hai.

Shift kya hai

Old paradigm me application ka center model hota tha — data model ko feed karta tha. New paradigm me center knowledge hota hai — knowledge graph model ko ground karta hai, LLM ko context deta hai, aur user ko explainable jawab deta hai. Model replace ho sakta hai, lekin knowledge rehta hai. Yahi shift enterprise AI ko production-ready banata hai: jab model badle, to knowledge dobara banana nahi padta.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 1 — Chapter 1

01.5Chapter 1 — Knowledge graphs and LLMs: A killer combination

KG aur LLM se application banana — use cases

Theory se pehle do real use cases dekh lete hain — ek drug discovery ka, ek customer support ka. Dono me KG aur LLM ka combination woh karta hai jo akeli technology nahi kar sakti.

Use case 1 — Drug discovery aur development

Nayi dawa banana 10+ saal aur billions of dollars ka kaam hai. Drug repurposing — purani dawa ko nayi bimari ke liye use karna — is cost ko bahut kam kar sakta hai. Knowledge graph drugs, diseases, genes aur proteins ke beech ke relationships ko ek jagah laata hai. Phir graph algorithms batate hain ki kaunsi dawa kis bimari ke liye candidate ho sakti hai — jaise Chapter 4 me Hetionet dataset par dikhaya gaya hai. LLM is analysis ko interpret karta hai: pathway results ko plain language me samjhata hai, aur researcher ko naye hypotheses suggest karta hai.

Use case 2 — Conversational AI for customer support

Customer support chatbot ko company ke products, policies aur procedures ka accurate knowledge chahiye hota hai. Sirf LLM par bharosa karo to woh confident galat jawab dega — jaise galat refund policy bata dega. KG me products, policies aur unke relationships structured form me hote hain. User ka sawaal pehle KG se grounded context retrieve karta hai, phir LLM us context se jawab banata hai. Jawab accurate bhi hota hai aur source ke saath verifiable bhi.

KG use karna hai ya nahi — decide kaise karein

Har problem ke liye KG zaroori nahi hai. Book teen sawaal poochhne ko kehti hai. Data connected hai? Agar entities ke beech relationships hi value hain, to KG sahi hai. Knowledge badalti rehti hai? Agar domain knowledge frequently update hoti hai, to KG me update karna model retrain karne se sasta hai. Explainability chahiye? Agar jawab ka source batana zaroori hai, to KG ka explicit structure jeet ta hai. Teenon ka jawab haan hai, to KG invest karne layak hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 1 — Chapter 1
← PreviousData-driven applications me paradigm shiftNext →Knowledge graph technologies — taxonomy aur ontology
01.6Chapter 1 — Knowledge graphs and LLMs: A killer combination

Knowledge graph technologies — taxonomy aur ontology

Knowledge graph banane se pehle uski vocabulary tay karni padti hai: kaunsi entities hongi, unke beech kaunse relationships honge, aur kaunse rules apply honge. Is vocabulary ko taxonomy aur ontology kehte hain — aur inke bina graph sirf nodes ka dher hai.

Taxonomy — hierarchy

Taxonomy ek hierarchy hai — jaise "dawa" ke neeche "antibiotic", uske neeche ek specific drug. Yeh batata hai ki cheezein ek doosre se kaise related hain, parent-child terms me. Simple hai, lekin sirf hierarchy tak limited hai.

Ontology — poora meaning

Ontology taxonomy se aage jati hai. Yeh sirf hierarchy nahi, poora domain model hai: classes, unke properties, relationships ke types, aur constraints. Jaise biomedical ontology me "Drug TREATS Disease" ek allowed relationship hai, lekin "Drug TREATS Gene" nahi — ontology yeh rules define karti hai. OWL aur RDF Schema jaise standards ontology likhne ke liye use hote hain.

RDF ya LPG — kaunsa model

Knowledge graph ke do popular data models hain. RDF (Resource Description Framework) har fact ko triple ke roop me rakhta hai — subject, predicate, object — aur web standards par based hai. LPG (Labeled Property Graph) nodes aur relationships dono par properties allow karta hai, aur Neo4j jaise databases me use hota hai. Dono ke apne tradeoffs hain; book Chapter 3 me goal-driven tareeke se chunne ki guide deti hai. Is book ke examples LPG aur Neo4j par based hain.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 1 — Chapter 1

01.7Chapter 1 — Knowledge graphs and LLMs: A killer combination

KG aur LLM ko kaise sikhayein — book ka roadmap

Yeh book ek roadmap hai: pehle foundations, phir KG banana, phir ML on graphs, aur aakhir me KG-powered retrieval aur question answering. Har part pichhle part par khada hota hai.

Book ke 5 parts

  • Part 1 — Foundations (Ch 1–2): KG aur LLM kya hain, intelligent system kya hota hai, aur hybrid approach kyun.
  • Part 2 — KGs from structured data (Ch 3–4): apna pehla KG ontologies se banana, phir biomedical multi-source integration.
  • Part 3 — KGs from text (Ch 5–8): unstructured text se KG banana, LLM se extraction, aur named entity disambiguation.
  • Part 4 — ML on KGs (Ch 9–12): feature engineering, embeddings, GNNs, aur node classification / link prediction.
  • Part 5 — Retrieval with KGs and LLMs (Ch 13–15): KG-powered RAG, natural language se KG poochhna, aur LangGraph QA agent.

Kaise padhna hai

Har chapter me mental models hain — figures jo poori picture ek nazar me dikhate hain. Code examples Neo4j aur Python par based hain, aur book ke companion repo me poora code available hai. Jo chapters Early Release ki tarah partial hain, unka scope SPA me honestly bataya gaya hai. Is SPA ka goal simple hai: book band karke bhi sab kuch yaad rahe — har number, har example, har code snippet yahin hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 1 — Chapter 1

02.1Chapter 2 — Intelligent systems: A hybrid approach

Intelligence kya hai

Intelligent system banane se pehle samajhna hoga ki intelligence hai kya. Book ke hisaab se intelligence sirf calculate karna nahi hai — yeh environment ko samajhna, usse seekhna, reasoning karna, aur goals ke hisaab se action lena hai.

Intelligence ki definition

Ek intelligent system woh hai jo apne environment ko perceive karta hai, us perception se knowledge banata hai, us knowledge par reasoning karta hai, aur phir aisa action leta hai jo uske goals ke liye best ho. Yeh loop chalta rehta hai — har action se feedback milta hai, aur feedback se system seekhta hai.

Yeh definition isliye important hai kyunki yeh batati hai ki AI sirf prediction nahi hai. Prediction ek hissa hai; poora system perception, knowledge, reasoning aur action ka combination hai. Isi liye book me intelligent system ko ek mental model ke roop me dikhaya gaya hai — task/question, environment/context, knowledge acquisition, knowledge bases, reasoning engines, aur action/suggestion/answer, sab ek feedback loop me jude hue.

Intelligent systems ki categories

Book systems ko categories me baant ti hai — reactive systems jo sirf current input par react karte hain, aur woh systems jo memory, learning aur planning use karte hain. Aage ke chapters me jo Intelligent Advisory System (IAS) banega, woh sabse advanced category me aata hai: woh user ko woh insights deta hai jo user khud extract nahi kar sakta — jaise researcher ko drug repurposing ke opportunities, ya clinician ko personalized treatment plan.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 2 — Chapter 2
← PreviousKG aur LLM ko kaise sikhayein — book ka roadmapNext →Intelligent system design karna — mental model
02.2Chapter 2 — Intelligent systems: A hybrid approach

Intelligent system design karna — mental model

Intelligent system ka mental model ek flow hai: user ka task ya sawaal aata hai, system environment aur context ko dekhta hai, knowledge acquire karta hai, knowledge bases me store karta hai, reasoning engines us par reasoning karte hain, aur aakhir me action, suggestion ya answer nikalta hai. Feedback loop har step ko behtar banata hai.

Model ke components

  • Task / Question: user kya chahta hai — sawaal, analysis, recommendation.
  • Environment / Context: system kahan chal raha hai, kaunsa data available hai, kaunse constraints hain.
  • Knowledge acquisition: raw data ko structured knowledge me convert karna.
  • Knowledge bases: converted knowledge ka store — KG ya LLM ke parameters, ya dono.
  • Reasoning engines: knowledge par logic lagakar naya insight nikalna.
  • Action / Suggestion / Answer: user ko milne wala output.
  • Feedback loop: user ki feedback aur environment se seekhna.

Characteristics — achha intelligent system kaisa hota hai

Book achhe intelligent system ki characteristics batati hai: woh apne domain ko samajhta hai, uncertainty handle karta hai, apne decisions ko explain kar sakta hai, naye data se seekhta hai, aur user ke goals ke hisaab se adapt karta hai. Yeh characteristics hi decide karti hain ki system me KG chahiye, LLM chahiye, ya dono — aur kis ratio me.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 2 — Chapter 2
← PreviousIntelligence kya haiNext →Knowledge acquisition aur representation
02.3Chapter 2 — Intelligent systems: A hybrid approach

Knowledge acquisition aur representation

Knowledge acquisition woh process hai jisse system apne domain ke data se "seekhta" hai — raw data ko structured knowledge me convert karta hai jo reasoning ke kaam aaye. KG aur LLM is process ko bilkul alag tareeke se karte hain, aur yahi farak poori book ki jaan hai.

KG ke liye acquisition — explicit aur expert-driven

KG ke liye acquisition ka matlab hai raw, structured ya semistructured data ko graph format me convert karna — entities nodes banti hain, relationships edges bante hain. Domain ka structure — ontology ya schema — is transformation ko guide karta hai. Is process me aksar ek domain expert ki zaroorat padti hai jo data ki semantics samajhta hai. Heterogeneous sources ko ek unified, explicit schema me convert karna meticulous kaam hai, lekin is preparation ka payoff flexibility me milta hai.

Domain expert KG acquisition me teen jagah madad karta hai: relevant data sources identify karna, data model ko support karna, aur results ko evaluate karna. Knowledge base ko domain experts manually bhi bana sakte hain aur machine-readable format me formalize kar sakte hain. Aur kyunki KGs human-readable hain, experts knowledge base ko validate bhi kar sakte hain.

LLM ke liye acquisition — implicit aur statistical

LLM knowledge acquire karta hai vast amounts of unstructured text ko ingest karke, jo training ke dauraan dense, high-dimensional vector spaces me encode ho jata hai. KG ke opposite, LLM ko extensive data preparation ki zaroorat nahi hoti, aur process mostly unsupervised hota hai — main effort data sources select karne aur cleaning me lagta hai. Information explicit relationships ki jagah statistical patterns ke roop me encode hoti hai.

Is implicit approach se LLM subtle contextual meanings aur complex linguistic relationships ko grasp kar leta hai, lekin knowledge opaque ho jata hai — use inspect ya modify karna mushkil hota hai. Domain expert sirf data source selection aur result evaluation par validate kar sakta hai; model ke andar jhank kar kuch badal nahi sakta. Fine-tuning hi ek support hai jo expert de sakta hai.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: KG me knowledge explicit hai — dekh sakte ho, badal sakte ho, validate kar sakte ho. LLM me knowledge implicit hai — powerful hai, lekin black box hai. Hybrid system dono ka fayda uthata hai.
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 2 — Chapter 2
← PreviousIntelligent system design karna — mental modelNext →Reasoning — deductive, inductive, abductive
02.4Chapter 2 — Intelligent systems: A hybrid approach

Reasoning — deductive, inductive, abductive

Reasoning woh process hai jisse existing knowledge se naya knowledge nikala jata hai. Book teen tarah ki reasoning batati hai — deductive, inductive aur abductive — aur har ek ka apna use case aur apni limit hai.

Deductive reasoning — rules se conclusion

Deductive reasoning me general rules se specific conclusions nikale jate hain. Jaise agar rule hai "har drug jo gene X ko bind karti hai, disease Y ke liye candidate hai", aur fact hai "drug D gene X ko bind karti hai", to conclusion hai "drug D disease Y ke liye candidate hai". KG par deductive reasoning natural hai — rules explicit hain, aur har conclusion trace kiya ja sakta hai. Lekin pure deductive engine ki limits hain: rules likhna mushkil hai, incomplete knowledge par woh chup rehta hai, aur uncertain data handle nahi karta.

Inductive reasoning aur ML — examples se pattern

Inductive reasoning examples se general patterns infer karta hai. Machine learning isi ka statistical version hai — bahut saare examples dekh kar model pattern seekhta hai aur naye cases par predict karta hai. Yeh incomplete aur noisy data par bhi kaam karta hai, lekin uske conclusions probabilistic hote hain — guarantee nahi hoti.

Abductive reasoning — best explanation

Abductive reasoning observations ke liye sabse achhi explanation dhoondhta hai — jaise doctor symptoms dekh kar sabse likely diagnosis sochta hai. Intelligent advisory systems me yeh bahut kaam aata hai: user ke sawaal aur available evidence se sabse plausible hypothesis banana.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 2 — Chapter 2
← PreviousKnowledge acquisition aur representationNext →Reasoning engines — KG rules vs LLM reasoning
02.5Chapter 2 — Intelligent systems: A hybrid approach

Reasoning engines — KG rules vs LLM reasoning

Reasoning engine woh component hai jo knowledge base par reasoning chalata hai. KG-based engines aur LLM-based engines alag tareeke se sochte hain — aur dono ki apni taakat aur apni kamzori hai.

KG reasoning engine — explicit aur verifiable

KG par reasoning rules, graph algorithms aur queries se hoti hai. Deductive rules facts se naye facts infer karte hain. Graph algorithms — jaise shortest path, centrality, community detection — structure se insight nikalte hain. Har step explainable hai: kis rule se kya conclusion aaya, yeh dikhaya ja sakta hai. Limit yeh hai ki rules manually likhne padte hain, aur jo knowledge graph me nahi hai, us par reasoning nahi ho sakti.

LLM reasoning engine — flexible lekin opaque

LLM reasoning language ke through hoti hai — chain-of-thought prompting, few-shot examples, aur tool use se model step-by-step sochta hai. Yeh flexible hai: naye sawaal, naye domain, bina rules likhe. Lekin reasoning opaque hai — model ne kyun woh conclusion nikala, yeh verify karna mushkil hai. Aur hallucination ka risk hamesha rehta hai.

Dono ko jodna

Hybrid reasoning engine me LLM sawaal ko samajhta hai aur plan banata hai, KG us plan ko ground karta hai — relevant facts retrieve karke, constraints check karke, aur results verify karke. Is combination se reasoning flexible bhi rehti hai aur verifiable bhi. Book ke aage ke chapters — khaas taur par Chapter 13, 14 aur 15 — isi hybrid reasoning ko implement karte hain.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 2 — Chapter 2
← PreviousReasoning — deductive, inductive, abductiveNext →KG approach to IAS — CRISP-DM revisited
02.6Chapter 2 — Intelligent systems: A hybrid approach

KG approach to IAS — CRISP-DM revisited

Intelligent Advisory System (IAS) banana ek project hai — aur har project ko ek methodology chahiye hoti hai. Book CRISP-DM ko revisit karti hai, lekin KG ko center me rakh kar.

CRISP-DM — classic methodology

CRISP-DM (Cross-Industry Standard Process for Data Mining) ek proven project methodology hai: business understanding, data understanding, data preparation, modeling, evaluation, deployment — ek cycle jo repeat hota hai. Yeh methodology data mining projects ke liye bani thi, lekin book ise KG platforms ke liye adapt karti hai.

Revisited CRISP-DM — KG center me

Revisited version me KG knowledge base ka model hai aur poori process ka center hai. Business understanding se pata chalta hai ki kis domain knowledge ki zaroorat hai; data understanding se pata chalta hai ki kaunse sources available hain; data preparation me sources ko KG me convert kiya jata hai; modeling me KG par algorithms aur LLM integration hoti hai; evaluation me KG ki quality aur system ke answers check hote hain; deployment me system users tak pahunchta hai. Aur har cycle me KG aur behtar hota hai — naya knowledge add hota hai, purana refine hota hai.

Is approach ka fayda yeh hai ki KG ek living asset ban jata hai — project khatam hone par khatam nahi hota, balki har naye use case ke saath grow karta hai. Chapter 3 me hum isi methodology ke pehle steps ko hands-on karenge: apna pehla KG banana.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 2 — Chapter 2
← PreviousReasoning engines — KG rules vs LLM reasoningNext →Pehla KG banana — warmup: business aur data understanding
03.1Chapter 3 — Create your first knowledge graph from ontologies

Pehla KG banana — warmup: business aur data understanding

Pehla KG banane se pehle do sawaal poochhne hote hain: business ko kya chahiye, aur data me kya hai. Yeh warmup phase CRISP-DM ke pehle do steps hain — aur ise skip karna sabse badi galti hai.

Business aur domain understanding

Pehle domain ko samjho: kis problem ko solve karna hai, kaun use karega, kaunse sawaal jawab chahiye. Book ka example biomedical domain hai — drug aur disease ke beech ke relationships. Domain expert ke saath baith kar use cases define karo: "kaunsi dawa kis bimari ka ilaaj karti hai?" jaise sawaal, jinka jawab KG dega. Is phase me ontology ki pehli draft bhi banti hai — kaunsi entity types hongi, kaunse relationships allowed honge.

Data understanding

Phir data ko dekho: kaunse sources hain, kis format me hain, kitna complete hai, kitna clean hai. Structured data (tables), semistructured data (JSON, XML), unstructured data (text) — har type ki apni challenges hain. Is chapter me focus structured sources par hai — ontologies aur annotations se KG banana. Data profiling karo: kitne records hain, kya missing hai, kya duplicate hai. Jo data samajh me nahi aaya, use KG me daalna kachra daalne jaisa hai.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: KG project ka 80% kaam data understanding aur preparation me hai, 20% loading aur querying me. Warmup skip karoge to graph banega, lekin galat graph banega.
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 3 — Chapter 3
← PreviousKG approach to IAS — CRISP-DM revisitedNext →KG technologies samajhna — RDF ya LPG?
03.2Chapter 3 — Create your first knowledge graph from ontologies

KG technologies samajhna — RDF ya LPG?

KG banane ke liye pehle technology choose karni hoti hai: data model kya hoga, database kaunsa hoga, aur ontology kaise represent hogi. Yeh decision goal-driven honi chahiye — technology pehle, problem baad me, yeh ulta hai.

RDF ya LPG — goal-driven discussion

RDF har fact ko triple me rakhta hai (subject–predicate–object) aur web standards (URIs, SPARQL) par based hai. Yeh tab best hai jab data ko web par share karna hai, alag-alag sources ko link karna hai, ya reasoning standards (OWL) chahiye hain. LPG nodes aur relationships dono par properties allow karta hai, aur Cypher jaise intuitive query language ke saath aata hai. Yeh tab best hai jab application development tez chahiye, properties rich hain, aur graph algorithms chalane hain.

Book LPG aur Neo4j choose karti hai — kyunki examples application-focused hain aur Cypher seekhna asaan hai. Lekin decision framework dono ke tradeoffs batata hai, taaki apne project ke liye sahi choice kar sako.

Edge properties — RDF vs LPG me farak

Edge par property rakhna LPG me natural hai — jaise DRIVES relationship par "since: 2020" property. RDF me yeh karne ke liye reification chahiye hoti hai — relationship ke baare me ek aur triple banana padta hai, jo verbose ho jata hai. Yeh chhota sa farak bade graphs me bahut bada ho jata hai. Agar tumhare relationships par rich metadata hai — dates, confidence scores, sources — to LPG zyada convenient hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 3 — Chapter 3
← PreviousPehla KG banana — warmup: business aur data understandingNext →KG banana — ontology aur annotation ingestion
03.3Chapter 3 — Create your first knowledge graph from ontologies

KG banana — ontology aur annotation ingestion

Ab hands-on: ontology ko Neo4j me load karna, aur annotations ko graph me convert karna. Is chapter me neosemantics (n10s) plugin ka use hota hai — jo RDF/OWL ontologies ko Neo4j me import karta hai.

Ontology ingestion — neosemantics se

Neosemantics ek Neo4j plugin hai jo ontologies ko graph me import karta hai. Process simple hai: ontology file (OWL/RDF) ko import karo, classes nodes banti hain, relationships edges bante hain, aur properties attach hoti hain. Import ke baad ontology khud graph ka hissa ban jati hai — schema aur data ek hi jagah rehte hain. Yeh KG ki khaasiyat hai: schema alag document me nahi, graph ke andar hai.

CALL n10s.graphconfig.init();
CALL n10s.onto.import.fetch(
  "https://example.org/ontology.owl", "RDF/XML");

Annotation ingestion aur processing

Ontology load hone ke baad data aata hai — annotations, jo batate hain ki kaunsi entity kis class ki hai aur unke beech kya relationships hain. Annotation files (CSV, JSON, RDF) ko parse karke nodes aur relationships banaye jate hain. Har entity ko ontology ki class se link kiya jata hai — taaki graph sirf data nahi, meaning bhi rakhe. Ingestion ke dauraan data cleansing bhi hoti hai: duplicates merge, missing values handle, aur formats normalize.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: Ontology pehle, data baad me. Bina schema ke data daaloge to graph banega lekin query karna mushkil hoga — har node ka type pata nahi hoga, har relationship ka matlab pata nahi hoga.
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 3 — Chapter 3
← PreviousKG technologies samajhna — RDF ya LPG?Next →Data ko query karna — Cypher
03.4Chapter 3 — Create your first knowledge graph from ontologies

Data ko query karna — Cypher

KG ban gaya — ab use poochho. Cypher Neo4j ki query language hai: pattern likho, graph woh pattern dhoond kar dega. SQL me joins likhne ki jagah, Cypher me graph ka shape draw karo.

Cypher basics

Cypher me pattern ASCII-art jaisa dikhta hai: (a:Drug)-[:TREATS]->(d:Disease) ka matlab hai "koi drug jo kisi disease ko treat karta hai". MATCH se pattern dhoondho, WHERE se filter karo, RETURN se result lo. Nodes ke liye round brackets, relationships ke liye square brackets aur arrow — pattern dekh kar hi samajh aata hai kya poochha ja raha hai.

MATCH (d:Drug)-[:TREATS]->(dis:Disease)
WHERE dis.name = "Asthma"
RETURN d.name AS drug, d.description AS info;

Aggregation aur analytics queries

Cypher me aggregation bhi asaan hai: COUNT, COLLECT, ORDER BY, LIMIT — sab SQL jaisa. Jaise "har disease ke liye kitni drugs hain?" ek query me nikal sakte ho. Graph algorithms bhi Cypher se call hote hain — shortest path, centrality, community detection — jo Chapter 10 me detail me aayenge.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 3 — Chapter 3
← PreviousKG banana — ontology aur annotation ingestionNext →KG par reasoning karna
03.5Chapter 3 — Create your first knowledge graph from ontologies

KG par reasoning karna

KG sirf store nahi hai — woh reason bhi kar sakta hai. Ontology ke rules aur graph ki structure se naye facts infer kiye ja sakte hain jo explicitly store nahi kiye gaye the.

Ontology-based reasoning

Ontology me hierarchy hoti hai: agar "Antibiotic" ek "Drug" hai, aur ek entity "Antibiotic" hai, to woh automatically "Drug" bhi hai. Yeh inference ontology reasoner karta hai — har baar manually likhne ki zaroorat nahi. Transitive relationships bhi infer hote hain: agar A, B ka part hai aur B, C ka part hai, to A, C ka part hai. Yeh reasoning KG ko "smart" banata hai — data se zyada nikalta hai.

Graph-based reasoning

Graph ki structure se bhi reasoning hoti hai: path analysis se indirect relationships nikalte hain, similarity se naye links suggest hote hain, aur constraints se inconsistencies pakdi jati hain. Jaise agar ontology kehti hai ki ek drug ek hi disease ko treat karti hai, lekin graph me do dikh rahe hain, to data quality issue hai. Reasoning sirf naya knowledge nahi banata — purane knowledge ko validate bhi karta hai.

Is chapter ke baad tumhare paas ek kaam karta hua KG hai: ontology loaded, data ingested, queries chal rahe hain, aur reasoning ho rahi hai. Part 2 me hum isse bada karenge — multiple sources se, biomedical domain me.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 3 — Chapter 3
← PreviousData ko query karna — CypherNext →Biomedical knowledge graphs aur unke applications
04.1Chapter 4 — From simple networks to multisource integration

Biomedical knowledge graphs aur unke applications

Biomedical domain knowledge graph ka sabse rich use case hai — drugs, diseases, genes, proteins, symptoms, pathways: sab connected hain, aur har connection ka matlab hai. Is chapter me hum simple networks se shuru karke multisource integration tak jayenge.

Biomedical KG kyun special hai

Biomedicine me data bahut zyada hai aur bahut fragmented hai — har database apna hissa rakhta hai. Drug databases drugs ke baare me batate hain, gene databases genes ke baare me, disease databases diseases ke baare me. Lekin asli insight inke beech ke connections me hai: kaunsi drug kis gene ko affect karti hai, kaunsa gene kis disease se linked hai. Knowledge graph in fragments ko ek picture me jodta hai.

Applications — kahan kaam aata hai

  • Drug repurposing: purani dawa, nayi bimari — graph se candidates nikalna.
  • Drug discovery: naye targets aur pathways dhoondhna.
  • Clinical decision support: patient data aur literature ko jod kar treatment suggest karna.
  • Multi-omics analysis: genomics, proteomics aur clinical data ko ek saath dekhna.

Is chapter ke examples Hetionet dataset par based hain — ek public KG jo 19 public databases ko integrate karta hai, 50,000 se zyada nodes ke saath, drugs, diseases, genes aur symptoms ko cover karte hue.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 4 — Chapter 4
← PreviousKG par reasoning karnaNext →Multi-omic applications — PPI aur protein-disease networks
04.2Chapter 4 — From simple networks to multisource integration

Multi-omic applications — PPI aur protein-disease networks

Multi-omics ka matlab hai biology ki alag-alag layers ko ek saath dekhna — genes, proteins, diseases — aur unke beech ke connections se samajhna ki system kaise kaam karta hai. KG iske liye perfect tool hai.

PPI network se KG banana

PPI (protein-protein interaction) network batata hai ki kaunse proteins ek doosre se interact karte hain. Protein-disease network batata hai ki kaunse proteins kis disease se associated hain. Dono networks ko ek KG me merge karne se ek multi-layer graph banta hai jahan protein se protein, protein se disease, aur disease se disease tak paths ban sakte hain.

High-level analysis

KG banne ke baad high-level analysis hoti hai: kitne nodes hain, kitne relationships hain, degree distribution kaisa hai, kaunse nodes sabse connected hain (hubs), aur kaunse communities banti hain. Yeh analysis batati hai ki graph healthy hai ya nahi — jaise agar ek node ka degree bahut zyada hai, to woh hub hai aur analysis me uska khaas dhyaan rakhna hoga. Domain-specific analysis bhi hoti hai: jaise ek specific disease ke aas-paas ka subgraph nikal kar dekhna ki kaunse proteins aur drugs usse jude hain.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: Multi-omic KG ka power layers ko jodne me hai. Sirf PPI network dekhoge to sirf proteins dikhenge; disease layer jodne se pata chalta hai ki woh proteins kis bimari me matter karte hain.
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 4 — Chapter 4
← PreviousBiomedical knowledge graphs aur unke applicationsNext →Pharmaceutical applications — Hetionet deep analysis
04.3Chapter 4 — From simple networks to multisource integration

Pharmaceutical applications — Hetionet deep analysis

Hetionet ek biomedical knowledge graph hai jo 19 public databases ko integrate karta hai — 50,000 se zyada nodes, drugs, diseases, genes aur symptoms ke. Is section me hum iska deep analysis karte hain: drug repurposing ke candidates kaise nikale jate hain.

Hetionet ka structure

Hetionet me node types hain: Compound (drug), Disease, Gene, Anatomy, Pathway, Side Effect, Symptom, aur bhi. Relationship types hain: Compound BINDS Gene, Gene ASSOCIATES Disease, Compound TREATS Disease, Gene PARTICIPATES Pathway, aur bhi. Har relationship ka apna matlab hai, aur metapaths — relationships ki sequences — se naye insights nikalte hain.

Metapaths — drug repurposing ka core idea

Metapath ek pattern hai: jaise Compound–binds–Gene–associates–Disease (CbGaD). Agar ek compound ek gene ko bind karta hai, aur woh gene ek disease se associated hai, to compound us disease ke liye candidate ho sakta hai. Isi tarah Compound–downregulates–Gene–upregulates–Disease (CdGuD) ek aur metapath hai. In metapaths par paths gin kar aur unhe normalize karke (DWPC — degree-weighted path count, Chapter 10 me detail me) har compound-disease pair ko ek score milta hai. Top scores wale pairs repurposing candidates hote hain.

MATCH (c:Compound)-[:BINDS_CbG]->(g:Gene)
      -[:ASSOCIATES_DaG]->(d:Disease)
RETURN c.name AS compound, d.name AS disease,
       count(*) AS path_count
ORDER BY path_count DESC LIMIT 10;
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 4 — Chapter 4
← PreviousMulti-omic applications — PPI aur protein-disease networksNext →LLM-assisted pathway analysis interpretation
04.4Chapter 4 — From simple networks to multisource integration

LLM-assisted pathway analysis interpretation

Graph analysis numbers deti hai — lekin numbers ka matlab samajhna ek aur kaam hai. Yahan LLM kaam aata hai: pathway analysis ke results ko interpret karke, researcher ko plain language me samjhata hai.

Pathway analysis kya hai

Pathway ek biological process hai — jaise ek chain of reactions jo cell me hoti hai. Pathway analysis batati hai ki kaunse pathways ek disease ya drug response me active hain. Results tables aur p-values ke roop me aate hain — padhna mushkil, samajhna aur mushkil.

LLM ka role

LLM pathway analysis ke results ko input lekar ek narrative banata hai: kaunse pathways significant hain, unka biological matlab kya hai, aur woh drug ke mechanism se kaise judte hain. Yeh interpretation researcher ka time bachata hai aur naye hypotheses suggest karta hai. Lekin important baat: LLM interpretation ko hamesha KG se ground karna chahiye — LLM ko sirf woh pathways dikhao jo analysis me significant nikle, taaki woh hallucinate na kare. Yeh hybrid approach ka perfect example hai: graph analysis kare, LLM samjhaye.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 4 — Chapter 4
← PreviousPharmaceutical applications — Hetionet deep analysisNext →Clinical applications — LLM-guided decision support
04.5Chapter 4 — From simple networks to multisource integration

Clinical applications — LLM-guided decision support

Clinic me doctor ke paas patient ka data hai, literature hai, clinical trials hain, aur standard protocols hain — lekin in sab ko ek saath jod kar personalized treatment plan banana mushkil hai. KG aur LLM mil kar yeh kar sakte hain.

LLM-guided clinical decision support

System patient ke symptoms, DNA sequence, aur medical history ko KG se jodta hai — diseases, drugs, genes aur guidelines ka graph. Phir LLM is grounded context se treatment options suggest karta hai, har suggestion ke saath uska source aur reasoning. Doctor final decision leta hai — system advise karta hai, decide nahi karta. Yahi Intelligent Advisory System ka matlab hai.

Important caveats

Clinical domain me accuracy aur safety sabse important hain. LLM ka har suggestion KG se verifiable hona chahiye — kis guideline se aaya, kis study par based hai. Hallucinated treatment suggestion ka cost zindagi ho sakta hai. Isi liye clinical IAS me KG grounding optional nahi, mandatory hai. Book is use case ko Chapter 4 ke end me isiliye rakhti hai: yeh dikhane ke liye ki hybrid approach sirf academic nahi, real-world critical hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 4 — Chapter 4
← PreviousLLM-assisted pathway analysis interpretationNext →The archives challenge — unstructured text se KG
05.1Chapter 5 — Extracting domain-specific knowledge from unstructured data

The archives challenge — unstructured text se KG

Ab tak hum structured data se KG bana rahe the. Lekin duniya ka zyada tar knowledge unstructured text me hai — documents, emails, archives. Is chapter me hum text se KG banana seekhenge, ek real archives project ke saath.

Rockefeller Archive Center — problem

Book ka running example Rockefeller Archive Center hai — ek historical archive jisme letters, reports aur documents hain. Challenge yeh hai: hazaaron documents me log, organizations, jagah aur events chhupe hain, lekin woh text me locked hain. Researcher ko yeh jaanna hai ki kaun kisse connected tha — intellectual networks. Manual reading se yeh impossible hai; text se KG banana hi solution hai.

Challenge ke parts

Text se KG banane me teen badi challenges hain. Pehli — extraction: text se entities aur relationships nikalna. Doosri — disambiguation: same naam ke alag log, ya ek vyakti ke alag-alag naam — kaun kaun hai? Teesri — integration: extracted knowledge ko existing schema aur ontology se jodna. Is chapter me pehle do concepts cover hote hain; disambiguation Chapter 7 me detail me aata hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 5 — Chapter 5
← PreviousClinical applications — LLM-guided decision supportNext →Knowledge extraction ke key concepts — NER aur relation extraction
05.2Chapter 5 — Extracting domain-specific knowledge from unstructured data

Knowledge extraction ke key concepts — NER aur relation extraction

Text se KG banane ke do core steps hain: pehle entities pehchano (NER), phir unke beech ke relationships nikalo (relation extraction). Dono ke apne tareeke hain — traditional NLP se lekar LLMs tak.

Named Entity Recognition (NER)

NER text me entities dhoondhta hai aur unhe type deta hai — PERSON, ORGANIZATION, LOCATION, DATE, aur domain-specific types jaise DRUG ya DISEASE. Traditional NER statistical models ya rule-based systems use karta hai; modern NER transformer models use karta hai. Archives jaise historical text me NER mushkil hota hai — purani spellings, abbreviations, aur context ki kami.

Relation extraction

Entities milne ke baad unke beech ke relationships nikalne hote hain — kaun kiske liye kaam karta tha, kaunsi organization kis project se judi thi. Relation extraction ke tareeke: pattern-based (jaise "X, director of Y"), supervised ML (labeled examples se seekhna), aur LLM-based (prompt se relationships nikalna). Har tareeke ka apna tradeoff hai — accuracy, cost, aur effort me.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: NER sirf "kya hai" batata hai, relation extraction "kaise jude hain" batata hai. Dono ke bina KG nahi banta — sirf entities ki list banti hai, graph nahi.
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 5 — Chapter 5
← PreviousThe archives challenge — unstructured text se KGNext →LLM se KG banana — prompt engineering
05.3Chapter 5 — Extracting domain-specific knowledge from unstructured data

LLM se KG banana — prompt engineering

LLM text se KG banana ka sabse powerful naya tareeka hai — lekin sirf tab jab prompt sahi ho. Is section me prompt engineering ke examples aur guidelines hain, seedha book se.

LLM se extraction kaise karein

Process simple hai: text chunk + schema + instructions LLM ko do, aur structured output lo — entities aur relationships, JSON ya triples ke roop me. Schema dena zaroori hai — bina schema ke LLM apni marzi ke types banayega aur graph inconsistent ho jayega. Output ko hamesha validate karo: entities schema ke types me hain? Relationships allowed types me hain? Invalid output ko reject ya repair karo.

Prompt engineering guidelines

  • Schema explicit do: allowed entity types aur relationship types list karo.
  • Examples do (few-shot): 2-3 sahi extraction examples dikhao — accuracy bahut badhti hai.
  • Output format fix karo: JSON schema ya triple format specify karo, taaki parsing asaan ho.
  • Chunk size control karo: bahut bada chunk do to LLM details miss karega; bahut chhota do to context kho jayega.
  • Hallucination check karo: extracted entity text me actually hai ya nahi — grounding check zaroori hai.
Extract entities and relationships from the text below.
Allowed entity types: PERSON, ORGANIZATION, LOCATION, EVENT.
Allowed relationships: WORKS_FOR, LOCATED_IN, PARTICIPATED_IN.
Return JSON: {"entities": [...], "relationships": [...]}

Text: [document chunk]
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 5 — Chapter 5
← PreviousKnowledge extraction ke key concepts — NER aur relation extractionNext →Traditional NLP ya LLM — kya choose karein
05.4Chapter 5 — Extracting domain-specific knowledge from unstructured data

Traditional NLP ya LLM — kya choose karein

KG extraction ke liye traditional NLP aur LLM — dono options hain. Kaunsa choose karein, yeh task, data aur budget par depend karta hai. Book ek clear comparison deti hai.

Traditional NLP — kab best hai

Traditional NLP (statistical NER, rule-based extraction) tab best hai jab domain narrow hai, labeled data available hai, aur cost matter karta hai. Yeh fast hai, cheap hai, aur deterministic hai — same input par same output. Lekin naye domain ya naye entity types ke liye retraining chahiye hoti hai, aur complex language par accuracy kam hoti hai.

LLM — kab best hai

LLM tab best hai jab domain broad hai, labeled data nahi hai, ya relationships complex hain. Few-shot prompting se bina training ke shuru kiya ja sakta hai, aur LLM context samajhta hai — jaise historical text ki nuances. Lekin cost zyada hai, output non-deterministic ho sakta hai, aur hallucination ka risk hai. Isi liye production me dono ka hybrid common hai: LLM se extraction, traditional methods se validation.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: Yeh "ya to NLP, ya LLM" ka sawaal nahi hai. Best systems dono use karte hain — LLM breadth ke liye, traditional NLP precision aur cost ke liye.
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 5 — Chapter 5
← PreviousLLM se KG banana — prompt engineeringNext →Archive ko KG me transform karna — Rockefeller case study
06.1Chapter 6 — Building knowledge graphs with large language models

Archive ko KG me transform karna — Rockefeller case study

Chapter 5 ke concepts ko ab ek poori pipeline me dekhte hain: Rockefeller Archive Center ke documents se knowledge graph banana — graph modeling se lekar entity resolution tak.

Graph modeling

Pehle decide karo graph kaisa hoga: kaunsi node types (Person, Organization, Document, Event, Place), kaunse relationships (AUTHORED, WORKED_FOR, MENTIONED_IN, LOCATED_IN), aur kaunse properties (dates, roles, titles). Yeh modeling domain expert ke saath hoti hai — archive ke historians batate hain ki kya matter karta hai. Model ko metagraph ke roop me visualize kiya jata hai — ek graph jo graph ka schema dikhata hai.

Normalization aur cleansing

Archives ka data ganda hota hai: naam alag-alag spellings me, dates alag formats me, missing values. Normalization me sab ko ek format me laya jata hai — dates ISO format me, naam standard form me. Cleansing me duplicates aur errors hataye jate hain. Yeh step boring hai lekin sabse important hai — ganda data daaloge to ganda graph banega.

Graph-based entity resolution

Entity resolution ka matlab hai: alag-alag mentions me se pehchanna ki kaunsi mentions ek hi real entity ki hain. Graph-based approach me sirf naam nahi, poora neighborhood dekha jata hai — do mentions ek hi vyakti ki hain agar unke connections similar hain (same organization, same co-authors, same time period). Yeh traditional string matching se zyada accurate hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 6 — Chapter 6
← PreviousTraditional NLP ya LLM — kya choose kareinNext →Intellectual network analysis — graph ki value
06.2Chapter 6 — Building knowledge graphs with large language models

Intellectual network analysis — graph ki value

Archive ka KG ban gaya — ab usse kya pata chalta hai? Intellectual network analysis batati hai ki kaun kisse connected tha, kaunse log influential the, aur ideas kaise spread hue.

Networks se kya dikhta hai

Graph par network analysis chalao: centrality se pata chalta hai kaunse log sabse influential the; community detection se pata chalta hai kaunse groups bante the; temporal analysis se pata chalta hai networks time ke saath kaise badle. Historian ke liye yeh woh insights hain jo documents ko ek-ek karke padh kar kabhi nahi milte — poora network ek nazar me dikhta hai.

Example — kya mila

Rockefeller archive me network analysis se pata chala ki kuch log "bridges" the — alag-alag communities ko jodne wale. Kuch organizations hubs the — bahut saare log unse jude the. Aur kuch time periods me network density badhi — jo historical events se match karti thi. Yeh woh value hai jo KG deta hai: data se zyada, structure se insight.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 6 — Chapter 6
← PreviousArchive ko KG me transform karna — Rockefeller case studyNext →Rockefeller project ke next steps
06.3Chapter 6 — Building knowledge graphs with large language models

Rockefeller project ke next steps

KG ban gaya, analysis ho gayi — aage kya? Book project ke next steps batati hai, jo har KG project par apply hote hain.

Next steps

  • Aur sources jodna: archive ke baaki collections, external databases, aur published literature se graph enrich karna.
  • Disambiguation improve karna: Chapter 7 aur 8 ke NED techniques se entity resolution aur accurate banana.
  • Search aur exploration tools: researchers ke liye graph ko explore karne ka interface — conceptual search aur structured search (Chapter 7).
  • LLM integration: natural language se archive poochhna — Chapter 13, 14 aur 15 ka topic.

Yeh steps batate hain ki KG project kabhi "complete" nahi hota — woh grow karta hai. Har naya source, har naya use case graph ko aur valuable banata hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 6 — Chapter 6
← PreviousIntellectual network analysis — graph ki valueNext →LLM era me knowledge graphs ki value
06.4Chapter 6 — Building knowledge graphs with large language models

LLM era me knowledge graphs ki value

Kuch log poochhte hain: LLM aa gaya to KG ki kya zaroorat hai? Is section ka jawab hai: LLM era me KG ki value aur badh gayi hai, kam nahi hui.

LLM ko KG kyun chahiye

LLM ko grounded, verifiable, up-to-date knowledge chahiye hoti hai — aur yeh teeno KG deta hai. RAG systems me KG retrieval ko guide karta hai; agents me KG tools aur memory deta hai; evaluation me KG ground truth deta hai. Bina KG ke LLM sirf apne training data par bharosa karta hai — jo stale, incomplete aur unverifiable hai.

KG ko LLM kyun chahiye

Doosri taraf, LLM KG banana aur maintain karna asaan banata hai — text se extraction, schema mapping, aur natural language querying. Pehle KG banana expert ka kaam tha; ab LLM ki madad se domain experts khud KG bana aur use kar sakte hain. Dono technologies ek doosre ko amplify karti hain — isi liye book ka title "killer combination" hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 6 — Chapter 6
← PreviousRockefeller project ke next stepsNext →Recognition se disambiguation tak — NED kya hai
07.1Chapter 7 — Named entity disambiguation

Recognition se disambiguation tak — NED kya hai

NER batata hai ki text me koi entity hai; NED (Named Entity Disambiguation) batata hai ki woh entity kaun hai — knowledge base me kis exact entry se match karti hai. Recognition pehchan hai, disambiguation pehchan ko identity dena hai.

Problem — ek naam, kai matlab

"Apple" ek fruit bhi hai aur company bhi. Ek hospital ke documents me "Zika" ek virus hai, lekin kisi aur context me kuch aur ho sakta hai. Aur ek hi vyakti ke naam alag-alag spellings me likhe ho sakte hain. Disambiguation ke bina KG me galat links banenge — ek node me do alag entities mix ho jayengi, ya ek entity do nodes me split ho jayegi.

NED pipeline — teen steps

Standard NED pipeline teen steps ki hoti hai: mention detection (text me entity mentions dhoondhna), candidate generation (knowledge base se possible matches nikalna), aur candidate ranking/disambiguation (context dekh kar best match chunna). Har step ki apni challenges hain, aur Chapter 8 me hum is pipeline ko LLM se implement karenge.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 7 — Chapter 7
← PreviousLLM era me knowledge graphs ki valueNext →NED ko samajhna — kaise kaam karta hai
07.2Chapter 7 — Named entity disambiguation

NED ko samajhna — kaise kaam karta hai

NED ka core idea hai context: entity ka matlab uske aas-paas ke words aur uske knowledge base entry se tay hota hai. Is section me NED ke approaches hain — traditional se lekar LLM-based tak.

Traditional NED approaches

Traditional NED string similarity (naam kitna milta hai), popularity (kaunsi entry sabse common hai), aur context similarity (aas-paas ke words knowledge base entry se kitne milte hain) use karta hai. Collective disambiguation ek step aage jati hai — ek document ki saari entities ko ek saath disambiguate karna, kyunki woh ek doosre se related hoti hain. Jaise ek medical document me "Zika" aur us syndrome dono hain, to dono ka medical meaning hi sahi hai.

LLM-based NED

LLM-based NED context ko behtar samajhta hai — poora document, domain knowledge, aur subtle clues. LLM candidate entities ke descriptions padh kar decide kar sakta hai ki kaunsi entry sahi hai. Lekin LLM ko domain ontology chahiye hoti hai — bina ontology ke woh generic answers dega. Isi liye Chapter 8 me ontology ingestion pehla step hai.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: NED accuracy KG quality decide karti hai. Galat disambiguation se graph me galat links banenge, aur un galat links par jo bhi analysis hogi, woh bhi galat hogi.
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 7 — Chapter 7
← PreviousRecognition se disambiguation tak — NED kya haiNext →Domain-based NED aur LLMs
07.3Chapter 7 — Named entity disambiguation

Domain-based NED aur LLMs

Generic NED har domain me kaam nahi karta — medical text me "cold" ek bimari hai, weather report me temperature hai. Domain-based NED domain ontology aur domain knowledge use karke disambiguation ko accurate banata hai.

Domain ontology ka role

Domain ontology batati hai ki is domain me kaunsi entities hain, unke beech kya relationships hain, aur kaunse terms ka kya matlab hai. Medical domain me UMLS (Unified Medical Language System) aur SNOMED CT jaise bade ontologies hain — SNOMED CT me 450,000 se zyada concepts hain. In ontologies ko NED system me ingest karke, disambiguation domain-aware ho jati hai.

LLM + domain ontology

LLM ko domain ontology dekar uski disambiguation power aur badh jati hai. LLM ontology ke concepts aur unke descriptions padh kar decide karta hai ki mention kis concept se match karta hai. Yeh combination — LLM ki language understanding + ontology ki domain knowledge — hi Chapter 8 ka end-to-end system hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 7 — Chapter 7
← PreviousNED ko samajhna — kaise kaam karta haiNext →Business aur data understanding — SoHO use case
07.4Chapter 7 — Named entity disambiguation

Business aur data understanding — SoHO use case

Is chapter ka running use case SoHO hai — substances of human origin. Business aur data understanding se shuru karte hain, phir KG banate hain.

Business understanding — SoHO kya hai

SoHO (substances of human origin) woh substances hain jo human body se aati hain — blood, tissues, cells — aur medical treatments me use hoti hain. Inka regulation aur traceability critical hai: kaunsi substance kahan se aayi, kis patient ko di gayi, kya outcome raha. Use case definition me sawaal tay hote hain: "is substance se judi adverse events kaunsi hain?", "kaunse donors se kaunse recipients tak chain kya hai?"

Data understanding

Data do tarah ka hai: unstructured data — documents, reports, literature jisme SoHO ke baare me likha hai; aur domain ontologies — UMLS aur SNOMED CT, jo medical concepts aur unke relationships define karte hain. Data understanding me yeh check kiya jata hai: documents me kaunse terms use hote hain, ontologies me woh terms kaise map hote hain, aur kya gaps hain.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 7 — Chapter 7
← PreviousDomain-based NED aur LLMsNext →SoHO knowledge graph banana
07.5Chapter 7 — Named entity disambiguation

SoHO knowledge graph banana

Ab SoHO KG banate hain: schema define karna, documents process karna, medical entities disambiguate karna, ontologies load karna, aur co-occurrences generate karna.

Steps

  • Schema define karna: kaunsi node types (Substance, Donor, Recipient, Adverse Event, Procedure), kaunse relationships (DERIVED_FROM, ADMINISTERED_TO, CAUSED).
  • Documents process aur ingest karna: text se entities extract karna (Chapter 5 ke tareeke se).
  • Medical entities disambiguate karna: har mention ko UMLS/SNOMED concept se link karna — NED pipeline.
  • Ontologies load aur map karna: UMLS aur SNOMED CT ko Neo4j me load karna, aur unke concepts ko KG se jodna.
  • Entity co-occurrences generate karna: jo entities ek document me saath aati hain, unke beech co-occurrence relationships banana — yeh discovery ka base hai.

Result ek KG hai jisme documents, medical concepts, aur unke beech ke links hain — aur jise query kiya ja sakta hai, explore kiya ja sakta hai, aur naye knowledge ke liye analyze kiya ja sakta hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 7 — Chapter 7
← PreviousBusiness aur data understanding — SoHO use caseNext →KG-based use cases — conceptual search aur discovery
07.6Chapter 7 — Named entity disambiguation

KG-based use cases — conceptual search aur discovery

SoHO KG ban gaya — ab isse kya kar sakte hain? Chaar use cases: conceptual search, structured search, interpretability, aur naye knowledge ki discovery.

Conceptual search

Conceptual search me user ek concept se search karta hai — jaise "Zika virus" — aur system woh documents aur entities deta hai jo conceptually related hain, sirf keyword match nahi. Graph traversal se related concepts milte hain: Zika se us neurological syndrome tak ka path, jo literature me co-occur karte hain. Keyword search "Zika" likhne par sirf woh documents deta hai jinme yeh word hai; conceptual search woh bhi deta hai jo concept se juda hai.

Structured knowledge-based search

Structured search me user graph ki structure se search karta hai — jaise "woh saare adverse events dikhao jo is substance se linked hain aur is time period me hue". Yeh Cypher queries se hota hai, aur results precise hote hain.

Interpretability aur discovery

KG-based interpretability ka matlab hai: har result ke peeche ka reason dikhana — kis path se yeh result aaya, kaunse documents support karte hain. Aur discovery ka matlab hai: graph me aise patterns dhoondhna jo pehle kisi ne notice nahi kiye — jaise do concepts ke beech ka unexpected connection jo nayi research direction de sakta hai. Book me Zika aur us neurological syndrome ka example hai: co-occurrence analysis se unka link saaf dikha, jo pehle obvious nahi tha.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 7 — Chapter 7
← PreviousSoHO knowledge graph bananaNext →Traditional NED systems ki limitations
08.1Chapter 8 — NED with open LLMs and domain ontologies

Traditional NED systems ki limitations

Traditional NED systems kaam karte hain, lekin unki limits hain — aur yahi limits LLM-based NED ko justify karti hain. Is chapter me hum open LLMs aur domain ontologies se NED banate hain.

Kya kami hai traditional systems me

  • Context ki kami: traditional systems sirf aas-paas ke kuch words dekhte hain; poora document ka context use nahi karte.
  • Domain adaptation mushkil: naye domain ke liye naye rules ya nayi training chahiye hoti hai.
  • Ambiguity handle nahi: jab do candidates barabar lagte hain, to traditional system popularity par bharosa karta hai — jo domain me galat ho sakta hai.
  • Explanation nahi: system ne yeh match kyun chuna, yeh batana mushkil hai.

LLM-based NED in sab ko address karta hai: poora context samajhta hai, few-shot se naye domain me adapt hota hai, aur apne decision ki reasoning de sakta hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 8 — Chapter 8
← PreviousKG-based use cases — conceptual search aur discoveryNext →Domain ontology ko ingest karna
08.2Chapter 8 — NED with open LLMs and domain ontologies

Domain ontology ko ingest karna

LLM-based NED ka pehla step hai domain ontology ko system me daalna — taaki LLM ko pata ho ki is domain me kaunse concepts hain aur unka kya matlab hai.

Ontology ingestion

SNOMED CT jaise ontology ko Neo4j me load kiya jata hai — 450,000 se zyada concepts, unke descriptions, synonyms, aur relationships. Har concept ka ek ID hota hai, ek preferred term hota hai, aur synonyms hote hain. Ingestion me ontology ki hierarchy bhi preserve hoti hai — jaise "viral disease" ke neeche "Zika virus disease".

Ontology ko LLM ke liye taiyaar karna

LLM ko poori ontology nahi dikhayi ja sakti — bahut badi hai. Isliye ontology ko aise format me taiyaar kiya jata hai jisse candidate selection me use ho sake: har concept ka embedding, ya search index, taaki mention ke liye relevant candidates quickly nikale ja sakein. Yeh retrieval step NED pipeline ka doosra hissa hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 8 — Chapter 8
← PreviousTraditional NED systems ki limitationsNext →Ollama aur Llama 3.1 8B se model setup
08.3Chapter 8 — NED with open LLMs and domain ontologies

Ollama aur Llama 3.1 8B se model setup

Is chapter ka system open LLM par chalta hai — Llama 3.1 8B, Ollama ke through. Open model ka matlab hai: data tumhare machine par rehta hai, cost predictable hai, aur customization possible hai.

Setup

Ollama ek tool hai jo LLMs ko locally run karna asaan banata hai. Llama 3.1 8B ek 8-billion-parameter model hai — kaafi capable, lekin ek achhe laptop ya workstation par chal sakta hai. Setup steps: Ollama install karo, model pull karo (ollama pull llama3.1:8b), aur Python se Ollama API ke through call karo.

import ollama

response = ollama.chat(
    model="llama3.1:8b",
    messages=[
        {"role": "system",
         "content": "You are a medical entity disambiguation assistant."},
        {"role": "user", "content": prompt},
    ],
)
answer = response["message"]["content"]

Open model kyun

Medical data sensitive hota hai — use third-party API par bhejna har organization ke liye possible nahi hai. Local open model se data ghar par rehta hai. Aur cost bhi: API calls ke per-token charges ki jagah, ek baar hardware cost. 8B model accuracy aur speed ka achha balance hai — bade model se behtar accuracy, chhote model se tez inference.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 8 — Chapter 8
← PreviousDomain ontology ko ingest karnaNext →End-to-end NED process — NER, candidate selection, disambiguation
08.4Chapter 8 — NED with open LLMs and domain ontologies

End-to-end NED process — NER, candidate selection, disambiguation

Ab poori pipeline: text aata hai, entities nikalti hain, candidates select hote hain, aur best match disambiguate hota hai. Teen phases, ek flow.

Phase 1 — Named entity recognition

LLM ya scispaCy jaise biomedical NER tool se text me medical entities detect hoti hain. scispaCy biomedical text ke liye specialized spaCy models deta hai — jo medical terms ko pehchanne me general models se behtar hai. Har mention ka text span aur type milta hai.

Phase 2 — Candidate selection

Har mention ke liye ontology se candidate concepts nikale jate hain — string matching aur embedding similarity se. Jaise "Zika" mention ke liye candidates ho sakte hain: Zika virus, Zika virus disease, Zika virus infection. Top-k candidates shortlist hote hain — aam taur par 5 se 10.

Phase 3 — Candidate disambiguation

LLM har candidate ka description aur mention ka context padh kar best match chunta hai — aur apni reasoning bhi deta hai. Output ek linked entity hoti hai: mention + ontology concept ID + confidence. Results October 2024 me evaluate kiye gaye: system ne traditional baselines se behtar accuracy dikhayi, khaas taur par ambiguous mentions par.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: Teen phases alag hain, lekin pipeline ek hai. NER galat hoga to candidates galat honge; candidates galat honge to disambiguation ka chance hi nahi. Har phase ki quality final accuracy decide karti hai.
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 8 — Chapter 8
← PreviousOllama aur Llama 3.1 8B se model setupNext →Conclusions — LLM-based NED se kya seekha
08.5Chapter 8 — NED with open LLMs and domain ontologies

Conclusions — LLM-based NED se kya seekha

Chapter 8 ka conclusion: open LLM + domain ontology se NED practical hai, accurate hai, aur privacy-friendly hai. Lekin yeh magic nahi hai — iski apni limits hain.

Kya kaam kiya

End-to-end pipeline ne dikhaya ki Llama 3.1 8B jaise open model se medical NED production-quality ho sakta hai — bina data ko bahar bheje, bina expensive API ke. Domain ontology ingestion se accuracy badhi, aur LLM ki reasoning se ambiguous cases solve hue jo traditional systems miss karte the.

Kya dhyaan rakhna hai

  • Ontology quality: NED utna hi achha hai jitni ontology achhi hai. Incomplete ontology se candidates hi nahi milenge.
  • Evaluation: har domain me evaluate karo — ek domain ki accuracy doosre domain me guarantee nahi hai.
  • Human-in-the-loop: low-confidence disambiguations ko human expert ke paas bhejo — fully automatic mat karo.
  • Cost vs accuracy: bada model behtar accuracy de sakta hai, lekin slow aur expensive hai. Apne use case ke hisaab se balance karo.

Part 3 yahin khatam hota hai — text se KG banana, disambiguation, aur use cases. Part 4 me hum KG par machine learning karenge.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 8 — Chapter 8
← PreviousEnd-to-end NED process — NER, candidate selection, disambiguationNext →Graphs par machine learning — kyun alag hai
09.1Chapter 9 — Machine learning on knowledge graphs: A primer approach

Graphs par machine learning — kyun alag hai

Machine learning tables par kaam karta hai — rows aur columns. Lekin graph table nahi hai: nodes aur edges hain, structure hai, aur har node ka context uske neighbors hain. Isi liye ML on graphs ek alag branch hai.

Graph data kyun alag hai

Tabular data me har row independent hoti hai — ek row ka prediction doosri row par depend nahi karta. Graph me aisa nahi hai: ek node ka label uske neighbors se related hota hai. Fraud detection me ek account fraudster hai ya nahi, yeh is baat par depend karta hai ki woh kin accounts se connected hai. Yeh dependency hi graph ML ki jaan hai — aur challenge bhi.

Intelligent Advisory System me ML ki zaroorat

IAS me advising ka matlab hai woh insights dena jo user khud extract nahi kar sakta. Researcher ko drug repurposing ke opportunities kaise milein? Clinician ko personalized treatment plan kaise mile? Yeh sawaal ML algorithms ke bina answer nahi hote — aur yeh algorithms graph ko input lekar chalte hain. Chapters 9 se 12 isi realm me hain: pehle primer, phir feature engineering, phir embeddings aur GNNs, aur aakhir me do end-to-end applications.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 9 — Chapter 9
← PreviousConclusions — LLM-based NED se kya seekhaNext →Graphs par common ML tasks — 4 tasks
09.2Chapter 9 — Machine learning on knowledge graphs: A primer approach

Graphs par common ML tasks — 4 tasks

Graph ML ke chaar core tasks hain — node classification, link prediction, clustering, aur graph classification. Har task ka apna use case hai, aur har task ke liye alag approach hai.

1. Node classification

Har node ko ek label dena — jaise transaction graph me kaunsa account licit hai aur kaunsa illicit (Chapter 12 ka AML example), ya social network me kaunsa user fraudster hai. Node ke features aur uske neighborhood — dono use hote hain.

2. Link prediction (relationship prediction)

Do nodes ke beech link hoga ya nahi, yeh predict karna — jaise kaunsi drug kis disease ka ilaaj kar sakti hai (drug repurposing), ya user kaunsi movie pasand karega (Chapter 12 ka MovieLens example). Recommendation systems ka core task yahi hai.

3. Clustering aur community detection

Graph ko communities me baantna — jaise social network me friend groups, ya biomedical graph me related diseases ka cluster. Communities se structure samajh me aata hai aur naye patterns dikhte hain.

4. Graph classification

Poore graph ko ek label dena — jaise ek molecule toxic hai ya nahi, ya ek protein structure kis family ki hai. Yahan poora graph ek sample hota hai, aur task hai graph-level prediction.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 9 — Chapter 9
← PreviousGraphs par machine learning — kyun alag haiNext →Do approaches — collective classification vs feature engineering
09.3Chapter 9 — Machine learning on knowledge graphs: A primer approach

Do approaches — collective classification vs feature engineering

Graph ML implement karne ke do raaste hain: graph ko seedha ML algorithm ko do (collective classification), ya graph ko feature vectors me convert karke traditional ML use karo (feature engineering). Is book me doosra raasta focus hai.

Collective classification

Collective classification me algorithm seedha graph ko input leta hai — node features aur neighborhood relationships ko ek saath consider karke predictions karta hai. Koi intermediate step nahi hota. Graph neural networks isi family me aate hain — Chapter 11 me detail me.

Feature engineering approach

Doosre approach me pehle graph structure ko feature vectors me convert kiya jata hai — har node ya har relationship pair ke liye ek vector. Phir is vector par traditional ML algorithms chalte hain — logistic regression, random forest, ya deep learning. Main challenge yeh ban jata hai: aise features define karna jo nodes, edges, aur poore graph ki essential characteristics capture karein. Chapter 10 isi challenge ko solve karta hai.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: Dono approaches valid hain. Feature engineering transparent aur debuggable hai — har feature ka matlab pata hai. Collective classification powerful hai lekin opaque hai. Production me aksar dono ko compare karke decide kiya jata hai.
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 9 — Chapter 9
← PreviousGraphs par common ML tasks — 4 tasksNext →Feature engineering se GNN tak — aage ka roadmap
09.4Chapter 9 — Machine learning on knowledge graphs: A primer approach

Feature engineering se GNN tak — aage ka roadmap

Is chapter ke baad ka roadmap: Chapter 10 me manual aur semiautomated feature engineering, Chapter 11 me embeddings aur GNNs, Chapter 12 me do end-to-end applications. Har chapter pichhle par build hota hai.

Kya seekhna hai

  • Chapter 10: node features (degree, triangles, density, paths, centrality, PageRank), relationship features (metapaths, DWPC), aur ReFeX se semiautomated extraction.
  • Chapter 11: embeddings kya hain, encoder-decoder model, shallow embeddings, KG embeddings, message passing aur GNNs.
  • Chapter 12: AML me node classification aur MovieLens me link prediction — GCN, GAT aur SAGE ki comparison ke saath.

Book is part ko apni pichhli book ka extension batati hai — naye algorithms aur theories ke saath, khaas taur par GNNs jo pichhle kuch saalon me improve hue hain aur graphs par test kiye gaye hain, jaise LLMs par.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 9 — Chapter 9
← PreviousDo approaches — collective classification vs feature engineeringNext →Manual node features — degree, triangles, density
10.1Chapter 10 — Graph feature engineering: Manual and semiautomated approaches

Manual node features — degree, triangles, density

Node ko feature vector me convert karne ka sabse seedha tareeka hai uski structural properties ginna: kitne neighbors hain, kitne triangles me hai, neighborhood kitna dense hai. Yeh features simple hain, lekin bahut powerful hain — aur LLM inhe samajh kar graph par reasoning bhi kar sakta hai.

Fraud graph — running example

Is chapter ka example ek fraud network hai: nodes log hain, relationships unke beech ke connections hain, aur kuch log recognized fraudsters hain. Goal hai naye nodes ko classify karna — fraudster hai ya nahi. Har node ke liye ek feature vector banaya jata hai, local metrics se global metrics tak.

Degree

Degree ek node ke connections ki ginti hai — kitne neighbors hain. Fraud network me high-degree nodes hubs ho sakte hain — ya to bahut popular log, ya fraud ring ke coordinators. In-degree aur out-degree alag se bhi gin sakte hain, directed graphs me.

Triangles

Triangle teen nodes ka group hai jo sab ek doosre se connected hain. Agar A, B aur C ke beech A-B, A-C aur B-C — teeno relationships hain — to yeh ek triangle hai. Triangles batate hain ki neighborhood kitna tightly-knit hai. Fraud rings me triangles common hote hain — fraudsters ek doosre se connected hote hain.

Density

Density batati hai ki nodes ke beech connections kitne hain, total possible connections ke hisaab se. N nodes wale fully connected graph me total possible edges N(N-1)/2 hote hain. Density = actual edges / possible edges. High density matlab tightly connected community; low density matlab sparse network. Node ki egonet (uske immediate neighbors ka subgraph) ki density ek useful feature hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 10 — Chapter 10
← PreviousFeature engineering se GNN tak — aage ka roadmapNext →Paths aur centrality — geodesic, closeness, betweenness, PageRank
10.2Chapter 10 — Graph feature engineering: Manual and semiautomated approaches

Paths aur centrality — geodesic, closeness, betweenness, PageRank

Local metrics ke baad global metrics: node poore network me kahan khada hai, kitna central hai, aur kitni information usse hokar guzarti hai. Yeh features fraud detection me sabse zyada kaam aate hain.

Geodesic paths

Geodesic path do nodes ke beech ka shortest path hai. Har node ke liye gin sakte hain: kitne 1-hop paths hain (direct neighbors), kitne 2-hop paths, kitne 3-hop paths. Book ke fraud graph (Table 10.4) me har node A se J tak ke geodesic paths gin kar dikhaye gaye hain — jaise node A ke 1-hop paths 1, 2-hop paths 4, 3-hop paths kuch aur. Yeh numbers node ki reach batate hain.

Closeness centrality

Closeness batati hai ki node baaki sab nodes ke kitna kareeb hai — average shortest path distance ka inverse. High closeness matlab node poore network tak jaldi pahunch sakta hai — information spread karne me fast hai. Values 0 aur 1 ke beech normalize ki jati hain.

Betweenness centrality

Betweenness batati hai ki kitne shortest paths is node se hokar guzarte hain — node kitna bada "bridge" hai. Book ke fraud graph me betweenness values: A=104, B=24.67, C=0, D=13.83, E=0, F=6.167, G=35.3, H=9, I=65, J=0; aur aage K=20, L=0, M=0, N=34, O=63, P=0, Q=35, R=0, S=0, T=0. Node A (104) sabse bada bridge hai — use hatane se network tut jayega. Fraud investigation me high-betweenness nodes pehle check hote hain.

PageRank

PageRank Google ka famous algorithm hai: node important hai agar important nodes usse link karte hain. Fraud graph me PageRank se woh nodes milte hain jo influential hain — na sirf connected, balki influential logon se connected. Yeh features mil kar har node ka ek rich vector banate hain, jise logistic regression jaise classifier ko diya jata hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 10 — Chapter 10
← PreviousManual node features — degree, triangles, densityNext →Manual relationship features — metapaths aur DWPC
10.3Chapter 10 — Graph feature engineering: Manual and semiautomated approaches

Manual relationship features — metapaths aur DWPC

Nodes ke baad relationships ki baari: do nodes ke beech link hoga ya nahi, yeh predict karne ke liye relationship features chahiye hote hain. Biomedical example se samajhte hain — drug repurposing.

Node-based aur path-based features

Relationship features do tarah ke hote hain. Node-based: source aur destination nodes ke features ko combine karna — jaise unke degree, ya unke embeddings ka product. Path-based: source aur destination ke beech ke paths ko dekhna — kitne paths hain, kaunse metapaths follow karte hain, kitne lambe hain.

Metapaths aur DWPC

Hetionet example me compound aur disease ke beech metapaths gin kar features banaye jate hain — jaise CbGaD (Compound-binds-Gene-associates-Disease) aur CdGuD (Compound-downregulates-Gene-upregulates-Disease). Sirf paths ginna misleading ho sakta hai: high-degree nodes (jaise ek gene jo bahut saare processes me hai) naturally zyada paths me aayega. Isi liye DWPC (degree-weighted path count) use hota hai — har path ko uske nodes ke degrees se weight kiya jata hai, exponent -0.4 ke saath. DWPC high-degree bias ko kam karta hai aur meaningful paths ko highlight karta hai.

MATCH path = (c:Compound)-[:BINDS_CbG]->(g1:Gene)
      -[:PARTICIPATES_GpPW]->(pw:Pathway)
      <-[:PARTICIPATES_GpPW]-(g2:Gene)
      -[:ASSOCIATES_DaG]->(d:Disease)
RETURN d.name AS disease, count(path) AS path_count;
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 10 — Chapter 10
← PreviousPaths aur centrality — geodesic, closeness, betweenness, PageRankNext →Semiautomated feature extraction — LLM se Cypher generate karna
10.4Chapter 10 — Graph feature engineering: Manual and semiautomated approaches

Semiautomated feature extraction — LLM se Cypher generate karna

Manual feature engineering me domain knowledge chahiye hoti hai aur time lagta hai. Semiautomated approach me LLM madad karta hai — metapaths ke liye Cypher queries generate karke.

LLM se query generation

Prompt me metapaths likho — jaise "CbGaD (Compound-binds-Gene-associates-Disease) aur CdGuD (Compound-downregulates-Gene-upregulates-Disease) ke liye queries generate karo, {source compound} aur {destination disease} ke saath" — aur LLM Cypher queries likh dega. Phir Python code un queries ko chala kar final representation banata hai. Yeh approach manual effort ko bahut kam kar deta hai, lekin LLM ki generated queries ko hamesha validate karna chahiye — galat relationship type ya galat direction se galat features banenge.

Manual vs semiautomated — tradeoff

Manual approach deep insight deta hai — tumhe pata hai har feature ka matlab kya hai. Semiautomated approach fast hai aur scale karta hai. Best practice: LLM se draft lo, domain expert se review karwao, phir production me daalo. Yeh hybrid approach poori book ki theme hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 10 — Chapter 10
← PreviousManual relationship features — metapaths aur DWPCNext →ReFeX — recursive feature extraction
10.5Chapter 10 — Graph feature engineering: Manual and semiautomated approaches

ReFeX — recursive feature extraction

ReFeX (Recursive Feature Extraction) ek automated tareeka hai node features banane ka: node ke neighborhood ke features ko recursively aggregate karo, har iteration me aur door tak. Manual features ka knowledge, automation ki speed — dono milte hain.

ReFeX kaise kaam karta hai

ReFeX teen scales par kaam karta hai: local (node khud — degree jaise features), egonet (immediate neighbors — neighbors ke degrees ka sum aur mean), aur recursive (neighbors ke neighbors, har iteration me aur door). Har iteration me naye features bante hain — jaise neighbor_degree_sum aur neighbor_degree_mean.
