Book ke example me node A ke neighbors H, I, B, G, O, T ke degrees 2, 4, 3, 4, 3, 1 hain — sum 17, mean 2.83. Agli iteration me in neighbors ke neighbors ke features aggregate hote hain.

Implementation

ReFeX implementation me do parameters hain: max_iterations=2 (kitni door tak jana hai) aur correlation_threshold=0.95 (redundant features hatane ke liye — agar do features 95% se zyada correlated hain, to ek ko hata do). Yeh pruning important hai — recursive features bahut jaldi explode ho jate hain, aur correlated features model ko confuse karte hain. ReFeX ke baad har node ka ek compact, informative feature vector ready hota hai — jo Chapter 11 ke embeddings ka manual counterpart hai.

class ReFeX:
    def __init__(self, max_iterations=2,
                 correlation_threshold=0.95):
        self.max_iterations = max_iterations
        self.correlation_threshold = correlation_threshold
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 10 — Chapter 10
← PreviousSemiautomated feature extraction — LLM se Cypher generate karnaNext →Graph representation learning — embeddings kya hain
11.1Chapter 11 — Graph representation learning and graph neural networks

Graph representation learning — embeddings kya hain

Manual features banane me human expertise chahiye hoti hai aur woh scale nahi karte. Graph Representation Learning (GRL) deep learning se optimal representations — embeddings — automatically seekhta hai, seedha graph structure aur node attributes se.

Embedding kya hai

Embedding ek node (ya edge, ya poora graph) ka dense vector representation hai — aam taur par 64, 128 ya 256 dimensions ka. Similar nodes ke vectors paas hote hain, alag nodes ke door. Isse graph ML tabular ML jaisa ban jata hai: vectors par koi bhi ML algorithm chal sakta hai — classification, clustering, similarity search.

GRL ki teen generations

Field teen generations se guzra hai. Pehli generation — traditional graph embedding: mathematics aur computer science se — matrix factorization jaise tareeke. Doosri generation — shallow embeddings: Node2Vec jaise random-walk methods. Teesri generation — GNNs: neural message passing se seekhne wale models. Har generation pichhli ki limitations ko solve karti hai.

Euclidean vs non-Euclidean space

Zyada tar ML models Euclidean space me kaam karte hain — straight-line distances, Pythagoras theorem. Lekin graphs non-Euclidean hain — unka structure flat nahi hai. Hierarchical graphs (jaise taxonomies) hyperbolic space me behtar represent hote hain. Yeh geometric insight batata hai ki graph embeddings ke liye sirf vectors nahi, sahi space bhi chahiye hota hai.

Positional vs structural embeddings

Positional embeddings node ki global position capture karte hain — graph me woh kahan hai. Yeh unsupervised tasks me useful hain — link prediction aur clustering. Structural embeddings node ki local role capture karte hain — woh apne neighborhood me kya karta hai. GNNs structural embeddings seekhte hain aur supervised tasks me excel karte hain.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 11 — Chapter 11
← PreviousReFeX — recursive feature extractionNext →Encoder-decoder model — embeddings ka unified framework
11.2Chapter 11 — Graph representation learning and graph neural networks

Encoder-decoder model — embeddings ka unified framework

Encoder-decoder model graph embedding methods ko samajhne ka unified tareeka hai: pehle graph ko encode karo (vectors me), phir decode karo (graph properties reconstruct karo). Translation system jaisa — encode, phir decode.

Encoder — graph se vectors

Encoder graph structure ko compact, standardized representations me convert karta hai. Shallow methods me encoder ek lookup table hai — har node seedha ek vector se map hota hai. GNNs me encoder message passing se vectors banata hai — neighbors ki information aggregate karke.

Decoder — vectors se graph properties

Decoder vectors se graph properties reconstruct karta hai — jaise do nodes ke beech edge hai ya nahi (link prediction), ya node ka label kya hai (node classification). Encoder aur decoder ko jointly train kiya jata hai: achha embedding woh hai jisse decoder graph ko accurately reconstruct kar sake.

Node2Vec — example

Node2Vec encoder-decoder ka classic example hai. Pehle graph par random walks kiye jate hain — breadth-first (broad, alag social circles explore karna) aur depth-first (deep, tight-knit groups me rehna) ke balance ke saath. Phir walks se seekha jata hai ki kaunse nodes aksar paas aate hain — unke vectors similar hote hain. Decoder phir in vectors se similarity ya link prediction karta hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 11 — Chapter 11
← PreviousGraph representation learning — embeddings kya hainNext →Shallow embeddings — pehla approach, aur uski limits
11.3Chapter 11 — Graph representation learning and graph neural networks

Shallow embeddings — pehla approach, aur uski limits

Shallow embeddings encoder-decoder ka sabse simple implementation hai: encoder ek lookup table hai jo har node ko seedha ek vector deta hai. Simple hai, lekin iski teen badi limitations hain.

Kaise kaam karta hai

Har node ke liye ek vector randomly initialize karo, phir training me use update karo taaki graph structure preserve ho — jaise connected nodes ke vectors paas aayein. Node2Vec aur DeepWalk isi family ke hain. Karate club network jaise chhote graphs par yeh bahut achha kaam karta hai — instructor (node 0) aur uske close ally (node 1) ke vectors similar hote hain, administrator (node 33) se door.

Teen limitations

  • Transductive hai: sirf training me dekhe gaye nodes ke liye embeddings hain. Naya node aaye to poora model dobara train karna padta hai — inductive learning nahi hai.
  • Node features use nahi karta: sirf structure dekhta hai; node ke attributes (jaise age, type, text) ignore karta hai.
  • Parameters bahut hain: har node ke liye alag vector — bade graphs me millions of parameters, sirf embeddings ke liye.

In limitations ne GNNs ko janm diya — jo features use karte hain, parameters share karte hain, aur naye nodes par bhi kaam karte hain.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 11 — Chapter 11
← PreviousEncoder-decoder model — embeddings ka unified frameworkNext →Knowledge graph embeddings — multiple relationship types
11.4Chapter 11 — Graph representation learning and graph neural networks

Knowledge graph embeddings — multiple relationship types

Simple graphs me ek tarah ka edge hota hai. Knowledge graphs me dozens of relationship types hote hain — TREATS, CAUSES, BINDS, ASSOCIATES. KG embeddings ko yeh multirelational structure capture karni hoti hai.

Loss function — positive aur negative samples

KG embedding training me har true fact (jaise "aspirin treats headache") ke saath negative samples bhi hote hain — false facts (jaise "aspirin treats broken leg") jinhe model ko reject karna hai. Loss function positive score ko badhata hai aur negative score ko ghatata hai. Gamma (γ) naam ka multiplier negative samples ki importance control karta hai.

Decoders — kaunsa, kab

Translational decoders (TransE): relationship ko ek translation maante hain — head + relation ≈ tail. Simple aur fast hai, lekin complex patterns (one-to-many, symmetric) par struggle karta hai. Semantic matching decoders (DistMult, ComplEx): entities aur relationships ki similarity measure karte hain. ComplEx khaas hai kyunki woh complex numbers use karke asymmetric relationships ko elegantly handle karta hai — jaise "A treats B" ka ulta "B treats A" nahi hota. Decoder ka choice decide karta hai ki model kis tarah ke patterns seekh sakta hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 11 — Chapter 11
← PreviousShallow embeddings — pehla approach, aur uski limitsNext →Message passing aur GNNs — neural conversation
11.5Chapter 11 — Graph representation learning and graph neural networks

Message passing aur GNNs — neural conversation

Graph Neural Network (GNN) ka core idea hai neural message passing: nodes apne neighbors se messages lekar apni representation update karte hain, iteration ke baad iteration. Jaise log apne doston se baat karke seekhte hain, waise nodes apne neighbors se seekhte hain.

Message-passing framework

Har iteration me har node apne neighbors se messages receive karta hai, unhe aggregate karta hai, aur apni representation update karta hai. Kuch iterations ke baad har node ki representation uske multi-hop neighborhood ki information capture karti hai — 2 layers matlab 2-hop tak ki information. Yeh framework powerful hai kyunki woh graph structure ko model ke andar le aata hai — model ko structure manually encode nahi karna padta.

Basic GNN model

Basic GNN me node u ki representation iteration k par update hoti hai: apni purani representation (self weight se) aur neighbors ki aggregated representation (neighbor weight se) ko combine karke, phir ek nonlinear activation (σ) lagakar. Parameters har iteration me share kiye ja sakte hain ya alag-alag train kiye ja sakte hain. Self-loops bhi add kiye jate hain — taaki node apni khud ki information na bhoole.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 11 — Chapter 11
← PreviousKnowledge graph embeddings — multiple relationship typesNext →Generalized aggregation, update aur GNN-LLM synergy
11.6Chapter 11 — Graph representation learning and graph neural networks

Generalized aggregation, update aur GNN-LLM synergy

Basic message passing se aage: neighborhoods alag sizes ke hote hain, kuch neighbors zyada important hote hain, aur deep networks me information kho jati hai. Is section me woh generalizations hain jo GNNs ko production-ready banati hain.

Neighborhood normalization

Har node ke neighbors ki ginti alag hoti hai — kisi ke 2, kisi ke 200. Naive aggregation (sum) se high-degree nodes dominate karenge. Normalization se har neighbor ka contribution scale hota hai — jaise degree se divide karke. GCN isi normalization ka famous example hai.

Attention aur multihead attention

Graph Attention Networks (GAT) har neighbor ko alag weight dete hain — important neighbors zyada, irrelevant kam. Jaise transformers me har word baaki words par attend karta hai, waise GAT me har node apne neighbors par attend karta hai. Multihead attention kai independent attention mechanisms chalata hai — har head alag pattern capture karta hai, phir results combine hote hain.

Generalized update — skip connections

Update phase me GraphSAGE ka skip connections ka innovation tha — purani representation ko nayi ke saath jodna, residual connections ki tarah. Isse deep GNNs me information preserve hoti hai aur training stable rehti hai.

GNNs aur LLMs ki synergy

GNN structured data me best hai — local neighborhoods, global topology, node classification aur link prediction. LLM unstructured language me best hai — text samajhna, reasoning, generation. Dono ko jodne se woh system banta hai jo graph ki structure aur language ki flexibility — dono use karta hai. Yahi synergy poori book ka destination hai: Chapter 13-15 me yeh combination RAG aur QA agents me implement hoti hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 11 — Chapter 11
← PreviousMessage passing aur GNNs — neural conversationNext →Node classification — anti-money laundering (Elliptic dataset)
12.1Chapter 12 — Node classification and link prediction with GNNs

Node classification — anti-money laundering (Elliptic dataset)

Ab theory ko practice me dekhte hain: do end-to-end GNN applications. Pehli hai anti-money laundering — transaction graph me licit aur illicit nodes ko classify karna.

Elliptic dataset

Elliptic dataset Bitcoin transactions ka graph hai: nodes transactions hain, edges unke beech money flow hain. elliptic_txs_classes.csv me 203,769 rows hain — har node ka label: 0 licit, 1 illicit, ya 2 unknown. Edges file me source aur target node IDs hain. Goal hai unknown nodes ko classify karna — kaunsa transaction illicit hai.

Data preparation — PyTorch Geometric

Data preparation me pehle node IDs ko incremental IDs me map kiya jata hai, phir node features ka tensor banaya jata hai (original node ID column drop karke), aur phir homogeneous PyG graph banaya jata hai. Labels ko mask se filter kiya jata hai: known_mask woh nodes hain jinka label 0 ya 1 hai (known), unknown_mask woh hain jinka label 2 hai (unknown). Training, validation aur testing sets sirf known nodes se bante hain.

known_mask = (data.y == 0) | (data.y == 1)
unknown_mask = data.y == 2
node_features = torch.tensor(
    features.drop(columns=['txId']).values,
    dtype=torch.float)
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 12 — Chapter 12
← PreviousGeneralized aggregation, update aur GNN-LLM synergyNext →GCN vs GAT vs SAGE — AML results
12.2Chapter 12 — Node classification and link prediction with GNNs

GCN vs GAT vs SAGE — AML results

Teen GNN encoders — GCN, GAT aur SAGE — same data par train kiye gaye. Results saaf hain: SAGE sabse achha, GAT kareeb, GCN sabse peeche.

Architecture — encoder-decoder

Har model encoder-decoder architecture use karta hai: GNN encoder node representations banata hai, phir log_softmax unhe probabilities me convert karta hai — licit vs illicit. GAT model me multihead attention hai: GATConv layers, hidden_dim * num_heads se concatenated dimensions adjust hote hain. Teenon models same training setup par compare kiye gaye.

Results — precision, recall, F1

Validation dataset par precision, recall aur F1-score track kiye gaye. SAGE sabse accurate hai — precision me consistent, aur zyada tar licit aur illicit nodes ko sahi classify karta hai, minimal misclassifications ke saath. GAT bhi strong hai — SAGE ke kareeb accuracy, lekin illicit class me thodi zyada misclassifications. GCN sabse weak hai — illicit nodes ke liye lower precision aur recall, matlab woh licit aur illicit me farak karne me struggle karta hai. Conclusion: neighborhood sampling (SAGE) aur attention (GAT) is task par simple convolution (GCN) se behtar hain.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: Model choose karte waqt sirf accuracy mat dekho — illicit class ki recall dekho. Ek illicit transaction miss karna, ek licit ko galat flag karne se zyada mehenga hai.
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 12 — Chapter 12
← PreviousNode classification — anti-money laundering (Elliptic dataset)Next →Link prediction — MovieLens recommendations
12.3Chapter 12 — Node classification and link prediction with GNNs

Link prediction — MovieLens recommendations

Doosra application hai movie recommendations: users aur movies ke beech ke links predict karna — kaunsa user kaunsi movie pasand karega. Yeh heterogeneous graph hai: do node types, ek relationship type.

MovieLens dataset

MovieLens dataset me movies.csv (movieId aur genres — jaise movie 1: Adventure|Animation|Children|Comedy|Fantasy) aur ratings.csv (userId aur movieId) hain. Total 9,742 movies hain. Graph me user nodes aur movie nodes hain, aur "rates" edges unhe jodte hain. Reverse edges ("rev_rates") bhi add kiye jate hain taaki message passing dono directions me ho — users se movies tak, aur movies se users tak.

Data preparation — heterogeneous PyG graph

Rating edges ko training, validation aur testing sets me split kiya jata hai — bina overlap ke, taaki evaluation honest ho. Final graph me edge_index=[2, 90753] — matlab 90,753 rating edges — aur edge_label=[30249] — 30,249 labeled edges evaluation ke liye. Validation set ka edge_index size 80,670 hai, jo training edges ke barabar hai.

data["movie"].x = movie_feat
data["user", "rates", "movie"].edge_index = edge_index_user_to_movie
data = T.ToUndirected()(data)
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 12 — Chapter 12
← PreviousGCN vs GAT vs SAGE — AML resultsNext →Heterogeneous GNN aur results
12.4Chapter 12 — Node classification and link prediction with GNNs

Heterogeneous GNN aur results

Heterogeneous graph ke liye heterogeneous GNN chahiye: users aur movies ke liye alag embeddings, aur har relationship type ke liye alag message passing. PyTorch Geometric ka to_hetero homogeneous model ko heterogeneous me convert karta hai.

Architecture

Model me pehle MovieLensEmbedding user aur movie nodes ke embeddings banata hai, phir heterogeneous GNN (modified GraphGCN, GAT ya SAGE) message passing karta hai. to_hetero base model ko metadata (node types aur edge types) ke saath convert karta hai, taaki har edge type par sahi convolution lage.

Results aur lessons

Link prediction me bhi wahi pattern: SAGE aur GAT GCN se behtar karte hain — kyunki woh neighborhoods ko selectively aggregate karte hain. Heterogeneous setting me ek aur lesson hai: node types ko alag treat karna zaroori hai — user aur movie ki features alag hain, unhe ek hi tarah se process karna accuracy kharab karta hai. Is chapter ke baad tumhare paas do complete GNN pipelines hain — node classification aur link prediction — jo kisi bhi domain me adapt kiye ja sakte hain.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 12 — Chapter 12
← PreviousLink prediction — MovieLens recommendationsNext →AI agents — LLM ko useful banana
13.1Chapter 13 — Knowledge graph–powered retrieval-augmented generation

AI agents — LLM ko useful banana

2023 AI upheaval ka saal tha. 2022 ke end me GPT-3.5 ke release ne NLP ki duniya ko ulta kar diya — months tak custom datasets aur models banane ki jagah, thodi si clever prompt engineering se lagbhag koi bhi NLP application ban sakti thi. Lekin LLM powerful hai, production enterprise scenarios ke liye kaafi nahi hai. Isi gap se AI agents, unki libraries, aur LLMOps paida hue.

AI agent kya hai

AI agent ek aisa system hai jo LLM ko tools, memory aur planning ke saath use karta hai — sirf jawab nahi deta, kaam karta hai. Agent sawaal ko samajhta hai, decide karta hai ki kaunsa tool use karna hai (search, database, KG query), tool chalata hai, results dekhta hai, aur jab kaafi context mil jaye to jawab deta hai. Yeh loop — think, act, observe — agent ko single LLM call se zyada capable banata hai.

Agents kyun zaroori hain

Enterprise me sawaal simple nahi hote: "is quarter ki sales kyun giri?" — iska jawab ek document me nahi hai, kai sources ko jodna padta hai. Agent yeh kar sakta hai: pehle KG se relevant entities nikalo, phir database se numbers lao, phir LLM se analysis banao. Is chapter me hum aisa hi ek agent banate hain — KG-powered RAG system.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 13 — Chapter 13
← PreviousHeterogeneous GNN aur resultsNext →LLM se chatting — basics
13.2Chapter 13 — Knowledge graph–powered retrieval-augmented generation

LLM se chatting — basics

Agent banane se pehle basics: LLM se chat karna kya hota hai, aur chat interface ke peeche kya hota hai. Yeh section woh foundation hai jiss par aage ke RAG aur agent systems khade hain.

Chat ka flow

Chat me har turn me teen cheezein hoti hain: system prompt (model ko role aur rules batata hai), conversation history (pehle ke turns ka context), aur user ka naya message. Model in teeno ko dekh kar agla response generate karta hai. History badhti jati hai, to context window ka dhyaan rakhna padta hai — purani baatein summarize ya truncate karni padti hain.

Chatting ki limits

Plain chatting me model sirf apne training data par bharosa karta hai — tumhare private data ke baare me use kuch pata nahi hota. Tumhare company ke documents, tumhare KG, tumhare database — inke baare me sawaal poochho to model guess karega ya mana kar dega. Isi liye aage RAG aata hai: chat ko external knowledge se ground karna.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 13 — Chapter 13
← PreviousAI agents — LLM ko useful bananaNext →Production environment ki challenges
13.3Chapter 13 — Knowledge graph–powered retrieval-augmented generation

Production environment ki challenges

Demo me LLM chat karna asaan hai; production me use chalana mushkil hai. Is section me woh challenges hain jo enterprise deployment me aati hain — aur unke solutions.

Challenges

  • Hallucination: galat jawab ka business cost — customer support me galat policy, finance me galat number.
  • Data privacy: private data ko third-party API par bhejna har organization ke liye possible nahi hai.
  • Cost aur latency: har sawaal par bada model call karna mehenga aur slow hai.
  • Evaluation: system sahi jawab de raha hai ya nahi, yeh measure karna mushkil hai — ground truth chahiye hoti hai.
  • Freshness: training data purana hai; nayi information kaise daalein bina retrain kiye.

In challenges ka solution ek hi pattern me hai: LLM ko external, verifiable knowledge se ground karo — aur woh knowledge KG se aata hai. Isi ko LLMOps kehte hain: LLMs ko production me reliably chalane ki practice.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 13 — Chapter 13
← PreviousLLM se chatting — basicsNext →Private data se chatting — RAG aur vector RAG ki limits
13.4Chapter 13 — Knowledge graph–powered retrieval-augmented generation

Private data se chatting — RAG aur vector RAG ki limits

Private data se chat karne ka standard tareeka hai RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation): sawaal se relevant documents retrieve karo, unhe LLM ko context ke roop me do, aur grounded jawab banao. Lekin vector-based RAG ki apni limits hain.

RAG kaise kaam karta hai

Documents ko chunks me todo, har chunk ko embed karo, vector database me index karo. Sawaal aaye to use embed karo, similar chunks retrieve karo, aur un chunks ke saath LLM ko prompt do. Jawab grounded hota hai — retrieved chunks par based. Yeh hallucination ko bahut kam kar deta hai.

Vector RAG ki limits

Vector search semantic similarity par kaam karta hai — lekin relationships nahi samajhta. "Kaunsi drug kis disease ka ilaaj karti hai?" jaise sawaal me sirf similar text kaafi nahi hai — drug aur disease ke beech ka relationship chahiye hota hai. Multi-hop sawaal ("is drug ke target gene se judi diseases kaunsi hain?") vector RAG se answer nahi hote — kyunki jawab ek chunk me nahi hai, kai chunks ko jodna padta hai. Aur global sawaal ("poori dataset me kaunse themes hain?") ke liye to vector search bilkul kaam nahi karta — use poori information ka summary chahiye hota hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 13 — Chapter 13
← PreviousProduction environment ki challengesNext →Graph RAG aur reasoning agents — KG se chatting
13.5Chapter 13 — Knowledge graph–powered retrieval-augmented generation

Graph RAG aur reasoning agents — KG se chatting

Vector RAG ki limits ko Graph RAG solve karta hai: retrieval ko graph structure se guide karo — entities, relationships, traversal aur community summaries ke saath. Aur reasoning agents is retrieval ko multi-step planning ke saath jodte hain.

Graph RAG

Graph RAG me documents se pehle KG banaya jata hai (Chapter 5-6 ke tareeke se). Sawaal aaye to pehle relevant entities aur subgraphs retrieve hote hain, phir unke aas-paas ka context expand hota hai — related nodes, relationships, aur communities. Communities ke summaries se global sawaal bhi answer hote hain. Result: jawab zyada complete, zyada accurate, aur explainable — kyunki har claim ka graph me source hai.

Reasoning agents

Reasoning agent ek step aage hai: woh sirf retrieve nahi karta, plan bhi banata hai. Complex sawaal ko chhote steps me todta hai, har step ke liye sahi tool chunta hai (vector search, KG query, ya dono), results ko check karta hai, aur jab kaafi context mil jaye to jawab deta hai. Is chapter ke end me "Let's chat with our KG" — ek working system jo KG se chat karta hai, RAG aur agent patterns ko combine karke.

Yaad rakhne wali baat: Graph RAG vector RAG ko replace nahi karta — dono saath kaam karte hain. Vector search semantic relevance deta hai, graph structure aur reasoning deta hai. Hybrid retrieval hi best retrieval hai.
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 13 — Chapter 13
← PreviousPrivate data se chatting — RAG aur vector RAG ki limitsNext →Policing domain me KG querying
14.1Chapter 14 — Asking a KG questions with natural language

Policing domain me KG querying

Is chapter me hum ek law enforcement example se advanced question-answering seekhenge: RAG approach aur naye "expert emulation" method ki comparison, domain experts ki expertise ko capture karke.

Domain — policing

Police ke paas bahut saara data hai — case files, reports, person records, locations, events — aur in sab ka ek KG ban sakta hai. Domain experts (experienced investigators) is KG se sawaal poochhte hain: "is vyakti se jude saare cases kaunse hain?", "is area me is time period me kaunse events hue?" Lekin experts ko Cypher nahi aati — unhe natural language me poochhna hai. System ka kaam hai natural language ko sahi query me badalna aur results ko actionable tareeke se present karna.

Framework ke pillars

  • Question routing: alag-alag tarah ke sawaal ko alag tareeke se handle karna.
  • Domain knowledge representation: knowledge ko aise form me rakhna jo LLM effectively use kar sake.
  • Expert-like reasoning: expert jaise query construction patterns implement karna.
  • Actionable presentation: results ko meaningful, actionable tareeke se dikhana.
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 14 — Chapter 14
← PreviousGraph RAG aur reasoning agents — KG se chattingNext →RAG for KG querying — capabilities aur challenges
14.2Chapter 14 — Asking a KG questions with natural language

RAG for KG querying — capabilities aur challenges

KG ko natural language se poochhne ka pehla approach hai RAG: sawaal se relevant context retrieve karo, LLM ko do, aur jawab banao. Lekin KG querying me RAG ki apni fragility hai.

RAG kab achha kaam karta hai

Jab context complete ho — sawaal ke liye zaroori saari information retrieved chunks me ho — to RAG achha jawab deta hai. Simple factual sawaal ("is vyakti ka address kya hai?") par RAG reliable hai.

RAG ki fragility

Lekin complex sawaal par RAG fragile ho jata hai. Agar retrieval me ek bhi zaroori chunk miss ho gaya, to jawab galat ya incomplete hoga — aur LLM ko pata bhi nahi chalega. Multi-hop sawaal, aggregation sawaal ("kitne cases...?"), aur comparison sawaal — in sab par RAG struggle karta hai. Aur jab context incomplete ho, to LLM gaps ko hallucination se bharta hai. Isi fragility se "expert emulation" method paida hua — jo RAG ki jagah expert ke reasoning patterns ko follow karta hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 14 — Chapter 14
← PreviousPolicing domain me KG queryingNext →Schema-based approach for KG querying
14.3Chapter 14 — Asking a KG questions with natural language

Schema-based approach for KG querying

Expert emulation ka pehla pillar hai schema-based approach: LLM ko graph ka schema dikhao, taaki woh sahi queries bana sake — guesswork ki jagah, structure ki madad se.

Schema kyun zaroori hai

LLM ko agar graph ka schema pata ho — kaunsi node types hain, kaunse relationships allowed hain, kaunse properties hain — to woh sahi Cypher queries generate kar sakta hai. Bina schema ke woh relationship types guess karega, jo aksar galat honge. Schema LLM ke liye map hai: kahan kya hai, kaise pahuncha jaye.

Schema extraction

Schema ko LLM-friendly format me present karna hota hai — sirf raw DDL nahi, balki descriptions ke saath: har node type kya represent karta hai, har relationship ka matlab kya hai, aur examples. Yeh schema extraction Chapter 15 ke pipeline ka ek step hai. Schema jitna clear hoga, queries utni sahi hongi.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 14 — Chapter 14
← PreviousRAG for KG querying — capabilities aur challengesNext →Expert jaise sochna — metadata ka use
14.4Chapter 14 — Asking a KG questions with natural language

Expert jaise sochna — metadata ka use

Expert investigators sirf data nahi dekhte — metadata bhi dekhte hain: kis source se data aaya, kab update hua, kitna reliable hai. Expert emulation method metadata ko reasoning ka hissa banata hai.

Metadata kya batata hai

Metadata batata hai: yeh fact kahan se aaya (source), kab ka hai (timestamp), aur kitna bharosemand hai (confidence). Expert in sab ko dekh kar decide karta hai ki kis evidence par bharosa karein. Jaise ek purana record aur ek naya record conflict karein to expert naye ko prefer karega — lekin purane ko bhi note karega.

Metadata se reasoning

System metadata ko query results ke saath jodta hai: har result ke saath uska source, date aur confidence dikhata hai. LLM in metadata ko dekh kar apni summary me caveats add karta hai — "yeh information 2023 ki hai, isliye verify kar lein" jaise. Yeh expert-like behavior hai: sirf jawab nahi, jawab ki reliability bhi batana.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 14 — Chapter 14
← PreviousSchema-based approach for KG queryingNext →Intent detection — user kya chahta hai
14.5Chapter 14 — Asking a KG questions with natural language

Intent detection — user kya chahta hai

Har sawaal ek jaisa nahi hota. Intent detection pehchanta hai ki user actually kya chahta hai — factual lookup, investigation, comparison, ya summary — aur us hisaab se system apna approach badalta hai.

Intent types

  • Factual lookup: ek specific fact chahiye — seedha query, seedha jawab.
  • Investigation: ek vyakti ya event ke aas-paas sab kuch explore karna — multi-step, graph traversal.
  • Comparison: do ya zyada entities ko compare karna — side-by-side analysis.
  • Aggregation: counts, trends, patterns — "kitne", "kab se", "kahan zyada".
  • Summary: poori picture ka narrative — LLM se summarization.

Intent se pipeline tak

Intent detect hone ke baad system decide karta hai: kaunsa query pattern, kitna context, kaunsa presentation format. Galat intent se galat approach — jaise investigation sawaal par sirf ek fact dena. Intent detection Chapter 15 ke LangGraph pipeline ka pehla step hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 14 — Chapter 14
← PreviousExpert jaise sochna — metadata ka useNext →LangGraph pipeline banana
15.1Chapter 15 — Building a QA agent with LangGraph

LangGraph pipeline banana

Ab sab kuch ek working application me jodte hain: LangGraph se orchestration, Streamlit se frontend — ek expert-emulating QA agent jo KG se natural language me baat karta hai.

Pipeline ke stages

System ka flow hai: Input (user request) → Intent detection (sawaal ko classify karo — factual, investigation, comparison, aggregation, summary) → Schema extraction (schema ko LLM-friendly format me banao) → Query generation (user input aur schema se formal queries banao) → Query execution (queries chalao, results lao) → Visualization (data ko graphs, tables ya aur formats me dikhao) → Summary (results ka summary banao aur analyze karo) → Output.

LangGraph kyun

LangGraph stateful, multi-step workflows ke liye bana hai — har stage ek node hai, aur transitions conditional hain. Jaise agar query execution fail ho, to pipeline wapas query generation par ja sakta hai — retry logic ke saath. Ya agar results khaali hain, to system user se clarification maang sakta hai. Yeh branching aur looping hi LangGraph ko simple chains se alag karta hai. Book ke code repo me complete implementation aur configuration files hain.

from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END

workflow = StateGraph(AgentState)
workflow.add_node("intent", detect_intent)
workflow.add_node("schema", extract_schema)
workflow.add_node("generate", generate_query)
workflow.add_node("execute", execute_query)
workflow.add_node("summarize", summarize_results)
workflow.set_entry_point("intent")
workflow.add_edge("intent", "schema")
workflow.add_edge("schema", "generate")
workflow.add_edge("generate", "execute")
workflow.add_edge("execute", "summarize")
workflow.add_edge("summarize", END)
app = workflow.compile()
Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 15 — Chapter 15
← PreviousIntent detection — user kya chahta haiNext →Streamlit application — frontend
15.2Chapter 15 — Building a QA agent with LangGraph

Streamlit application — frontend

Backend pipeline ready hai — ab users ko interface chahiye. Streamlit se ek simple, interactive frontend banta hai: sawaal poochho, results dekho, visualizations explore karo.

Streamlit app ka structure

App me teen hisse hain: input area — user apna sawaal likhta hai aur zaroorat pade to options select karta hai (jaise kaunsa intent, kaunsa time period); results area — query results tables, graphs aur charts me dikhte hain; summary area — LLM-generated summary aur analysis. Har step ka status bhi dikhta hai — intent kya detect hua, kaunsi query bani, kitne results mile — taaki user ko system par trust ho.

Frontend design decisions

Book integration-first approach follow karti hai: frontend ko end users ke liye design kiya gaya hai, developers ke liye nahi. Isi liye har result ke saath uska source dikhta hai, har summary ke saath caveats dikhte hain, aur visualizations interactive hote hain. User ko yeh samajhna chahiye ki jawab kahan se aaya — yahi trust banata hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 15 — Chapter 15

15.3Chapter 15 — Building a QA agent with LangGraph

Expert-emulating investigation

Is section me poori investigation ka ek end-to-end example hai: ek sawaal se shuru karke, pipeline ke har step se guzarte hue, final actionable summary tak.

Investigation ka flow

Example: investigator poochhta hai ek vyakti ke baare me. Intent detection kehta hai: yeh investigation hai, factual lookup nahi. Schema extraction relevant node types aur relationships nikalta hai. Query generation kai queries banata hai — vyakti ke cases, associates, locations, timeline. Execution results lata hai. Visualization network graph dikhata hai — vyakti center me, associates aas-paas. Summary LLM likhta hai: key findings, patterns, aur next steps ke suggestions — metadata aur caveats ke saath.

Kya alag hai is approach me

Normal RAG is sawaal par ek paragraph deta. Expert-emulating system ek investigation deta hai: structured evidence, visual network, aur reasoned summary. Farak yeh hai ki system expert ke workflow ko follow karta hai — pehle evidence collect karo, phir analyze karo, phir conclude karo — sirf generate mat karo.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 15 — Chapter 15

15.4Chapter 15 — Building a QA agent with LangGraph

Future directions aur enhancements

Book ke end me future directions hain — system ko aur behtar banane ke tareeke. Yeh list har QA agent project par apply hoti hai.

Enhancements

  • Multi-agent collaboration: alag-alag agents alag tasks ke liye — ek retrieval ke liye, ek reasoning ke liye, ek verification ke liye.
  • Memory: past conversations aur investigations ko yaad rakhna, taaki follow-up sawaal context ke saath answer hon.
  • Evaluation frameworks: system ki accuracy ko automatically measure karna — ground-truth QA pairs se.
  • Human feedback loop: user corrections se system seekhe — queries aur summaries improve hon.
  • Bigger graphs, faster queries: scale badhane par performance optimization — indexing, caching, aur query optimization.

Book yahin khatam hoti hai — lekin tumhara kaam yahin se shuru hota hai. Foundations (Part 1), KG building (Part 2-3), ML (Part 4), aur retrieval (Part 5) — sab mil kar ek poora toolkit hai intelligent advisory systems banane ka.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Chapter 15 — Chapter 15

A.1Appendix A — Introduction to graphs

Graphs ka introduction — Königsberg bridges

Graph ek simple aur purana mathematical concept hai: vertices (nodes) aur edges (relationships) ka set, jo objects ke beech ke relationships model karta hai. Is appendix me graph ki duniya ke key concepts hain.

Königsberg aur saat bridges

Kehte hain ki 1736 me ek mathematician ne graphs ke baare me baat shuru ki thi — woh Königsberg (Prussia, ab Kaliningrad, Russia) me the, aur zyada chalna nahi chahte the. Sheher Pregel River ke dono kinaron par tha, do bade islands ke saath, jo ek doosre se aur mainland se saat bridges se jude the. Problem formalize ki gayi: kya har bridge ko exactly ek baar cross karke poora sheher ghooma ja sakta hai? Prove hua ki yeh impossible hai. Isi proof se graphs aur graph theory ka janm hua.

Formal definition

Formally, graph ek pair hai: G = (V, E), jahan V vertices ka collection hai aur E edges ka collection hai. Har edge do vertices ko jodta hai. Graph ko draw karne ka sabse simple tareeka hai: har vertex ke liye ek dot ya chhota circle, aur connected vertices ko line se jodo. Yeh simple structure hi knowledge graphs ki foundation hai — nodes aur edges, bas scale aur meaning badh jati hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Appendix A — Chapter A
← PreviousFuture directions aur enhancementsNext →Neo4j — graph database
B.1Appendix B — Neo4j

Neo4j — graph database

Poori book ke examples, code aur exercises ek specific graph database par based hain: Neo4j. Theories, algorithms aur code kisi bhi graph database par adapt kiye ja sakte hain — lekin Neo4j ko isliye chuna gaya kyunki authors use andar se jaante hain, yeh native graph database hai, aur iski badi community hai.

Neo4j kya hai

Neo4j ek labeled property graph database hai, Java me implement kiya gaya hai. DB-Engines ke mutaabik Neo4j kai saalon se sabse popular graph DBMS hai. Do editions hain: Community Edition — GPL3-licensed, open source; aur Enterprise Edition — backup, scaling extensions aur enterprise features ke saath, closed source commercial terms par. Access transactional HTTP endpoint ya binary Bolt protocol ke through hota hai.

Cypher — query language

Cypher Neo4j ki declarative query language hai — pattern likho, graph woh pattern dhoond kar dega. Book me Cypher ke basics, plugins (jaise neosemantics), aur configuration cover hain. Cypher seekhna asaan hai kyunki patterns visual hain — (a)-[:REL]->(b) dekh kar hi samajh aata hai kya poochha ja raha hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Appendix B — Chapter B
← PreviousGraphs ka introduction — Königsberg bridgesNext →Structured sources se KG banana — microRNA case study
C.1Appendix C — Building knowledge graphs from structured sources

Structured sources se KG banana — microRNA case study

Is appendix me structured data sources se apna khud ka KG banana seekhenge — biomedical use case ke saath: microRNA disease associations ka detection.

Use case — microRNA aur disease

microRNAs chhote RNA molecules hain jo gene expression regulate karte hain — jaise hsa-mir-31, hsa-mir-5. Kuch microRNAs kuch diseases se associated hote hain — jaise celiac disease. Structured sources (databases aur spreadsheets) me yeh associations listed hain. Kaam hai inhe ek KG me convert karna: microRNA nodes, disease nodes, aur RELATED_TO relationships.

Process

Process Chapter 3 jaisa hi hai: sources ko samjho, schema define karo (microRNA, Disease, RELATED_TO), data ko map karo, Neo4j me load karo, aur phir query karo — jaise "celiac disease se judi saari microRNAs kaunsi hain?" Yeh appendix dikhata hai ki KG banana ke liye hamesha complex NLP nahi chahiye — structured data se bhi shuru kiya ja sakta hai, aur yahi aksar sabse achha starting point hota hai.

Source: Knowledge Graphs and LLMs in Action, Manning, Appendix C — Chapter C

FEnd Matter · FAQs

Interview FAQs

Knowledge graphs, LLMs, GNNs aur RAG par interview me poochhe jaane wale sawaal — poori book ke concepts par, Hinglish me.

Q01Knowledge graph kya hota hai, aur yeh relational database se kaise alag hai?
Knowledge graph information ko nodes (entities) aur relationships (unke beech ke connections) ke roop me represent karta hai, properties ke saath. Relational database me relationships ke liye expensive joins chahiye hote hain; graph database connections ko directly traverse karta hai, jisse deep connected data ki querying tez aur efficient hoti hai. Graph me relationships first-class citizen hote hain, tables me woh sirf foreign keys hote hain.
Q02LLM hallucinate kyun karta hai, aur knowledge graph isse kaise rokta hai?
LLM words me nahi, word vectors me sochta hai — woh text ko semantic chunks me tod kar statistical relationships map karta hai aur agla word predict karta hai. Jab specialized factual knowledge chahiye aur woh grounded na ho, to model confident dikhne wala galat jawab bana deta hai — yahi hallucination hai. Knowledge graph LLM ko grounded, verifiable context deta hai, jisse jawab retrieved facts par based hota hai aur hallucination kam hoti hai.
Q03RDF aur LPG me kya farak hai, aur kaunsa kab choose karein?
RDF har fact ko triple (subject-predicate-object) me rakhta hai aur web standards par based hai — data share karne, sources link karne aur OWL reasoning ke liye best hai. LPG nodes aur relationships dono par properties allow karta hai aur Cypher jaise intuitive language ke saath aata hai — application development aur rich metadata ke liye best hai. Edge par property rakhna LPG me natural hai, RDF me reification chahiye hoti hai.
Q04Ontology kya hai, aur taxonomy se kaise alag hai?
Taxonomy sirf ek hierarchy hai — parent-child terms, jaise dawa ke neeche antibiotic. Ontology usse aage jati hai: poora domain model — classes, unke properties, relationship types, aur constraints. Ontology batati hai ki kaunse relationships allowed hain, jaise Drug TREATS Disease allowed hai lekin Drug TREATS Gene nahi. OWL aur RDF Schema ontology likhne ke standards hain.
Q05Intelligent Advisory System (IAS) kya hota hai?
IAS ek aisa system hai jo user ko woh insights deta hai jo user khud extract nahi kar sakta — jaise researcher ko drug repurposing ke opportunities, ya clinician ko personalized treatment plan. Iska mental model hai: task/question, environment/context, knowledge acquisition, knowledge bases, reasoning engines, aur action/suggestion/answer — sab ek feedback loop me jude hue. System advise karta hai, decide nahi karta.
Q06KG aur LLM knowledge acquire karne me kaise alag hain?
KG knowledge explicitly acquire karta hai — structured data ko ontology-guided transformation se graph me convert karta hai, domain expert ki madad se. Knowledge human-readable aur modifiable hoti hai. LLM knowledge implicitly acquire karta hai — vast unstructured text ko training me dense vector spaces me encode karke, mostly unsupervised. Knowledge powerful hoti hai lekin opaque hoti hai — inspect ya modify karna mushkil hai.
Q07Deductive, inductive aur abductive reasoning me kya farak hai?
Deductive reasoning general rules se specific conclusions nikalta hai — jaise rule aur fact se nayi fact infer karna; yeh verifiable hai lekin incomplete knowledge par chup rehta hai. Inductive reasoning examples se patterns infer karta hai — machine learning isi ka statistical version hai, probabilistic conclusions ke saath. Abductive reasoning observations ke liye sabse achhi explanation dhoondhta hai — jaise doctor symptoms se diagnosis sochta hai.
Q08CRISP-DM kya hai, aur book ise KG ke liye kaise revisit karti hai?
CRISP-DM ek proven project methodology hai: business understanding, data understanding, data preparation, modeling, evaluation, deployment — ek cycle jo repeat hota hai. Book ke revisited version me knowledge graph poori process ka center hai: business understanding se pata chalta hai kis knowledge ki zaroorat hai, data preparation me sources KG me convert hote hain, modeling me KG par algorithms aur LLM integration hoti hai, aur har cycle me KG aur behtar hota hai.
Q09Neosemantics (n10s) kya hai, aur ontology import kaise karta hai?
Neosemantics ek Neo4j plugin hai jo RDF/OWL ontologies ko graph database me import karta hai. Process me ontology file import hoti hai, classes nodes banti hain, relationships edges bante hain, aur properties attach hoti hain. Import ke baad ontology khud graph ka hissa ban jati hai — schema aur data ek hi jagah rehte hain. Isse KG me data ke saath uska meaning bhi store hota hai.
Q10Cypher query kaise likhte hain? Ek simple example do.
Cypher me pattern ASCII-art jaisa dikhta hai: MATCH (d:Drug)-[:TREATS]->(dis:Disease) WHERE dis.name = 'Asthma' RETURN d.name. MATCH pattern dhoondhta hai, WHERE filter karta hai, RETURN result deta hai. Nodes round brackets me, relationships square brackets aur arrow se likhe jate hain. SQL me joins likhne ki jagah, Cypher me graph ka shape draw karo — pattern dekh kar hi samajh aata hai kya poochha ja raha hai.
Q11Hetionet kya hai, aur drug repurposing me kaise kaam aata hai?
Hetionet ek biomedical knowledge graph hai jo 19 public databases ko integrate karta hai — 50,000 se zyada nodes, drugs, diseases, genes aur symptoms ke. Drug repurposing me metapaths use hote hain — jaise Compound-binds-Gene-associates-Disease (CbGaD). Agar ek compound ek gene ko bind karta hai aur woh gene ek disease se associated hai, to compound us disease ke liye candidate ho sakta hai. Paths ko DWPC se score kiya jata hai.
Q12Metapath kya hai, aur DWPC kyun zaroori hai?
Metapath relationships ki ek sequence hai jo ek pattern define karti hai — jaise Compound-binds-Gene-associates-Disease. Sirf paths ginna misleading ho sakta hai kyunki high-degree nodes naturally zyada paths me aate hain. DWPC (degree-weighted path count) har path ko uske nodes ke degrees se weight karta hai, exponent -0.4 ke saath, taaki high-degree bias kam ho aur meaningful paths highlight hon.
Q13NER aur NED me kya farak hai?
NER (Named Entity Recognition) text me entities dhoondhta hai aur unhe type deta hai — jaise PERSON ya DISEASE. NED (Named Entity Disambiguation) batata hai ki woh entity kaun hai — knowledge base me kis exact entry se match karti hai. Recognition pehchan hai, disambiguation pehchan ko identity dena hai. NED pipeline ke teen steps hain: mention detection, candidate generation, aur candidate ranking.
Q14SNOMED CT aur UMLS kya hain, aur NED me kyun zaroori hain?
UMLS (Unified Medical Language System) aur SNOMED CT bade medical ontologies hain — SNOMED CT me 450,000 se zyada concepts hain, unke descriptions, synonyms aur relationships ke saath. NED me yeh domain knowledge dete hain: mention kis concept se match karta hai, yeh ontology batati hai. Bina domain ontology ke NED generic answers dega — medical text me 'cold' bimari hai, weather me temperature hai.
Q15Traditional NED ki limitations kya hain, aur LLM-based NED kaise behtar hai?
Traditional NED sirf aas-paas ke kuch words dekhta hai, naye domain ke liye retraining chahiye hoti hai, ambiguity par popularity par bharosa karta hai, aur apne decisions explain nahi kar sakta. LLM-based NED poora context samajhta hai, few-shot se naye domain me adapt hota hai, aur apni reasoning de sakta hai. Lekin use domain ontology chahiye hoti hai aur generated outputs ko validate karna padta hai.
Q16Ollama aur Llama 3.1 8B se NED system kaise setup karte hain?
Ollama ek tool hai jo LLMs ko locally run karna asaan banata hai. Llama 3.1 8B ek 8-billion-parameter open model hai jo achhe laptop ya workstation par chal sakta hai. Setup: Ollama install karo, model pull karo (ollama pull llama3.1:8b), aur Python se Ollama API ke through call karo. Local model se sensitive medical data ghar par rehta hai aur per-token API cost nahi lagti.
Q17Prompt engineering se KG extraction me kya dhyaan rakhna chahiye?
Schema explicit do — allowed entity aur relationship types list karo. Few-shot examples do — 2-3 sahi extraction examples se accuracy bahut badhti hai. Output format fix karo — JSON ya triples, taaki parsing asaan ho. Chunk size control karo — bahut bada chunk details miss karega, bahut chhota context kho dega. Aur extracted entities ko hamesha validate karo — entity text me actually hai ya nahi, yeh grounding check zaroori hai.
Q18Graphs par ML tabular ML se kaise alag hai?
Tabular data me har row independent hoti hai — ek row ka prediction doosri row par depend nahi karta. Graph me node ka label uske neighbors se related hota hai — fraud detection me account fraudster hai ya nahi, yeh is baat par depend karta hai ki woh kin accounts se connected hai. Yeh dependency hi graph ML ki jaan hai, aur isi liye collective classification aur feature engineering jaise alag approaches chahiye hote hain.
Q19Node classification, link prediction, clustering aur graph classification me kya farak hai?
Node classification har node ko label deti hai — jaise transaction licit hai ya illicit. Link prediction do nodes ke beech link hoga ya nahi, yeh predict karti hai — jaise drug-disease ya user-movie. Clustering graph ko communities me baant ti hai — jaise friend groups. Graph classification poore graph ko ek label deti hai — jaise molecule toxic hai ya nahi. Har task ka apna use case aur approach hai.
Q20Collective classification aur feature engineering me kaunsa behtar hai?
Collective classification me algorithm seedha graph ko input leta hai — node features aur neighborhood ko ek saath consider karke predict karta hai; GNNs isi family me aate hain. Feature engineering me pehle graph ko feature vectors me convert kiya jata hai, phir traditional ML chalta hai — logistic regression, random forest. Feature engineering transparent aur debuggable hai; collective classification powerful lekin opaque hai. Production me dono ko compare karke decide kiya jata hai.
Q21Degree, triangles aur density features kya batate hain?
Degree batata hai node ke kitne neighbors hain — hubs pehchanne me madad karta hai. Triangles batate hain neighborhood kitna tightly-knit hai — teen nodes jo sab ek doosre se connected hain. Density batati hai actual edges kitne hain, total possible edges ke hisaab se — N nodes ke liye possible edges N(N-1)/2 hote hain. Fraud rings me high triangles aur high density common hote hain.
Q22Betweenness centrality kya hai, aur fraud detection me kyun kaam aati hai?
Betweenness batati hai ki kitne shortest paths ek node se hokar guzarte hain — node kitna bada bridge hai. Book ke fraud graph me node A ki betweenness 104 hai — sabse zyada — matlab woh network ka sabse bada bridge hai; use hatane se network tut jayega. Fraud investigation me high-betweenness nodes pehle check hote hain kyunki woh money ya information ke flow ko control karte hain.
Q23ReFeX kya hai, aur yeh manual features se kaise alag hai?
ReFeX (Recursive Feature Extraction) automated tareeka hai node features banane ka: node ke neighborhood ke features ko recursively aggregate karo, har iteration me aur door tak. Local features (degree), egonet features (neighbors ke degrees ka sum aur mean — jaise node A ke liye sum 17, mean 2.83), aur recursive features — teen scales. Parameters hain max_iterations=2 aur correlation_threshold=0.95, jo redundant features hatata hai.
Q24Graph embeddings kya hain, aur shallow embeddings ki limits kya hain?
Embedding ek node ka dense vector representation hai — similar nodes ke vectors paas hote hain. Shallow embeddings (Node2Vec, DeepWalk) me encoder ek lookup table hai — har node seedha ek vector se map hota hai. Inki teen limits hain: transductive hain (naye node par dobara training chahiye), node features use nahi karte, aur har node ke liye alag vector se parameters explode hote hain. Inhi limits ne GNNs ko janm diya.
Q25TransE, DistMult aur ComplEx decoders me kya farak hai?
TransE translational decoder hai — relationship ko translation maanta hai, head + relation lagbhag tail ke barabar; simple aur fast hai lekin complex patterns par struggle karta hai. DistMult aur ComplEx semantic matching decoders hain — similarity measure karte hain. ComplEx complex numbers use karke asymmetric relationships ko elegantly handle karta hai — jaise A treats B ka ulta B treats A nahi hota.
Q26Message passing GNN me kaise kaam karta hai?
Har iteration me har node apne neighbors se messages receive karta hai, unhe aggregate karta hai, aur apni representation update karta hai. Kuch iterations ke baad har node ki representation uske multi-hop neighborhood ki information capture karti hai — 2 layers matlab 2-hop tak ki information. Basic update rule me self weight aur neighbor weight dono hote hain, phir nonlinear activation lagti hai. Self-loops add kiye jate hain taaki node apni khud ki information na bhoole.
Q27GCN, GAT aur SAGE me kya farak hai, aur AML me kaunsa jeeta?
GCN neighborhood ko normalize karke aggregate karta hai — simple lekin har neighbor ko barabar weight deta hai. GAT attention use karta hai — important neighbors ko zyada weight, irrelevant ko kam; multihead attention kai patterns capture karta hai. SAGE neighbors ko sample karke aggregate karta hai — scalable hai. Elliptic AML dataset par SAGE sabse accurate raha, GAT kareeb, GCN sabse peeche — illicit nodes ki recall me GCN struggle karta hai.
Q28Elliptic dataset kya hai, aur AML me GNN kaise use hota hai?
Elliptic dataset Bitcoin transactions ka graph hai: nodes transactions hain, edges money flow hain. elliptic_txs_classes.csv me 203,769 rows hain — har node ka label 0 licit, 1 illicit, ya 2 unknown. GNN encoder node representations banata hai, log_softmax unhe probabilities me convert karta hai. Training sirf known nodes par hoti hai; unknown nodes ko classify karna goal hai.
Q29MovieLens link prediction me heterogeneous graph kyun zaroori hai?
MovieLens me do node types hain — users aur movies — aur ek relationship type, rates. Total 9,742 movies aur 90,753 rating edges hain. Homogeneous model dono node types ko ek jaisa treat karega, jo galat hai — user aur movie ki features alag hain. Heterogeneous GNN (PyTorch Geometric ka to_hetero) har node type aur edge type ke liye alag processing karta hai, aur reverse edges se message passing dono directions me hoti hai.
Q30RAG kya hai, aur vector RAG ki limits kya hain?
RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) me documents ko chunks me tod kar embed kiya jata hai, sawaal se similar chunks retrieve kiye jate hain, aur un chunks ke saath LLM grounded jawab banata hai. Vector RAG ki limits: relationships nahi samajhta — multi-hop sawaal jinka jawab kai chunks ko jod kar banta hai, woh answer nahi kar sakta; aur global sawaal jinka jawab poori dataset ka summary hai, unke liye top-k chunks kaafi nahi hote.
Q31Graph RAG vector RAG se kaise behtar hai?
Graph RAG me documents se pehle KG banaya jata hai. Sawaal aaye to relevant entities aur subgraphs retrieve hote hain, context expand hota hai — related nodes, relationships, communities. Communities ke summaries se global sawaal bhi answer hote hain. Jawab zyada complete, zyada accurate aur explainable hota hai — har claim ka graph me source hai. Dono saath kaam karte hain: vector search semantic relevance deta hai, graph structure aur reasoning deta hai.
Q32AI agent kya hai, aur yeh simple LLM chat se kaise alag hai?
AI agent LLM ko tools, memory aur planning ke saath use karta hai — sirf jawab nahi deta, kaam karta hai. Agent sawaal samajhta hai, decide karta hai kaunsa tool use karna hai, tool chalata hai, results dekhta hai, aur jab kaafi context mil jaye to jawab deta hai. Simple chat sirf apne training data par bharosa karti hai; agent external tools aur knowledge se ground hota hai. 2022 ke end me GPT-3.5 ke release ke baad agents aur LLMOps enterprise AI ka focus ban gaye.
Q33Expert emulation method RAG se kaise alag hai?
RAG sawaal se relevant context retrieve karke LLM ko deta hai — lekin agar retrieval me ek zaroori chunk miss ho gaya to jawab galat hoga, aur LLM ko pata bhi nahi chalega. Expert emulation expert investigator ke reasoning patterns ko follow karta hai: schema-based querying, metadata ka use (source, date, confidence), intent detection, aur structured evidence ke saath actionable summary. Yeh RAG ki fragility ko address karta hai.
Q34LangGraph pipeline ke stages kya hain?
Pipeline ke stages hain: input (user request), intent detection (sawaal classify karo), schema extraction (schema ko LLM-friendly format me banao), query generation (formal queries banao), query execution (queries chalao), visualization (graphs, tables), summary (results ka summary aur analysis), aur output. LangGraph stateful workflows ke liye bana hai — agar query fail ho to pipeline wapas ja sakta hai, retry kar sakta hai, ya user se clarification maang sakta hai.
Q35Neo4j kya hai, aur book isse kyun use karti hai?
Neo4j ek labeled property graph database hai, Java me implement kiya gaya hai, aur DB-Engines ke mutaabik kai saalon se sabse popular graph DBMS hai. Community Edition GPL3-licensed open source hai; Enterprise Edition me backup aur scaling features hain. Access HTTP endpoint ya binary Bolt protocol se hota hai. Book Neo4j use karti hai kyunki authors use andar se jaante hain, yeh native graph database hai, aur Cypher query language seekhna asaan hai.
Q36Königsberg bridges ka graph theory se kya connection hai?
1736 me Königsberg sheher ke saat bridges ka problem formalize kiya gaya: kya har bridge ko exactly ek baar cross karke poora sheher ghooma ja sakta hai? Prove hua ki yeh impossible hai. Isi proof se graphs aur graph theory ka janm hua. Formally graph G = (V, E) hai — vertices aur edges ka pair. Yahi simple structure knowledge graphs ki foundation hai.
